title: The Door to Paradise
verses: For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God,
not a result of works, so that no one may boast.
story: In the summer of 1505, a young man named Martin Luther was walking home to his law school in Germany. His father wanted him to become a rich and important lawyer. Suddenly the sky turned black, and a terrible thunderstorm crashed down around him. A bolt of lightning struck so close that it threw Martin to the ground. Terrified that he was about to die and face God, he cried out, “Help me, Saint Anne! I will become a monk!”

Martin survived, and he kept his promise. Two weeks later, to his father’s great anger, he knocked on the door of a monastery and gave his whole life to God. But Martin had a big problem: he was afraid of God. He had been taught that God was a strict judge, and that he had to make himself good enough for heaven.

So Martin tried harder than anyone. He prayed for hours. He fasted until he was weak. He slept in a cold room with no blanket. He went to confession so often, sometimes for six hours at a time, that his teacher finally told him, “Martin, go out and commit a real sin, then come back!” But no matter how hard he tried, Martin never felt good enough. “I was a good monk,” he said later, “but my conscience would not give me peace.”

His wise teacher, Johann von Staupitz, gave him a new job: “Become a professor and teach the Bible.” So Martin began to study the Bible more closely than ever. One day, he was reading Romans 1:17: “The righteous shall live by faith.” He had read it many times, and he had always hated the words “the righteousness of God,” because he thought they meant God’s perfect standard that he could never reach.

But this time, he looked closer, and suddenly he understood. The righteousness of God isn’t something we have to earn. It’s something God gives to us, for free, because of Jesus. We are made right with God through faith, by trusting in what Jesus did on the cross, not by how hard we try. Martin said it felt like he had been born again, and that the doors of paradise had been thrown wide open.
From then on, Martin couldn’t stop telling people this good news. And on October 31, 1517, that good news would start a fire that spread across the whole world. But that is a story for next time.
teach: Lutherans sum it up in three short phrases: grace alone (God saves us as a free gift), faith alone (we receive it by trusting Jesus), and Scripture alone (God’s Word tells us so). That’s exactly what Ephesians 2:8–9 says.
We still try to obey God, but not to earn His love. We obey because we already have it.
q: What scared Martin in the storm? Do we have to earn God’s love, or is it a gift?
Why couldn’t Martin feel good enough, no matter how hard he tried? What changed when he read Romans 1:17?
Lots of people still think they have to be “good enough” for God. Why is grace such good news? If we’re saved by grace, why do we still try to do good?
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for opening Martin Luther’s eyes to the good news, and for giving us that same gift. Thank You that we don’t have to earn Your love, because Jesus earned it for us.
ask: When we feel like we’re not good enough, remind us that we are Yours by grace.

title: The Hammer and the Door
verses: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,
story: Remember how Martin Luther discovered that God’s forgiveness is a free gift? Well, not everyone was teaching that. In those days, the church needed money to build a giant new church in Rome called St. Peter’s. So church leaders began selling pieces of paper called indulgences. People were told that if they paid money, their sins, or the sins of a loved one who had died, would be forgiven.

A preacher named Johann Tetzel traveled from town to town selling them. He even had a catchy rhyme: “As soon as the coin in the box rings, the soul from purgatory springs!” Poor families gave money they couldn’t spare, hoping to buy God’s forgiveness. Some people in Luther’s own church came to confession waving their papers and said, “I don’t need to be sorry. I already paid.”

Luther was heartbroken and angry. He knew forgiveness can’t be bought. Jesus already paid for it with His own blood on the cross, and He gives it away for free. So Luther sat down and wrote ninety-five statements, called theses, explaining what was wrong with selling forgiveness. One of them said: “The true treasure of the church is the most holy gospel of the glory and grace of God.”

On October 31, 1517, the day before All Saints’ Day, Luther walked up to the big wooden door of the Castle Church in Wittenberg and nailed up his 95 Theses. Back then, the church door was like a town bulletin board. Luther only wanted the teachers and priests to discuss it. But people copied his words, translated them into German, and printed them on the brand-new printing press. In just a few weeks, people all over Germany were reading them.
Luther had no idea what he was starting. That’s why Lutherans celebrate October 31 as Reformation Day, the day the church began to be “re-formed” around the good news of Jesus.
teach: Romans 3:24 says we are justified “by his grace as a gift.” A gift you pay for isn’t a gift anymore. Jesus paid the whole price, so we receive forgiveness with empty hands.
That’s why we hear the words of absolution at church: “I forgive you all your sins.” It costs us nothing because it cost Jesus everything.
q: What did Luther nail to the church door? Can we buy God’s forgiveness with money?
Why was Luther so upset about indulgences? Why do you think his 95 Theses spread so fast?
What’s the difference between a gift and a payment? Where do people today still try to “pay” God back or earn His approval?
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for paying for all our sins on the cross, so that forgiveness is a free gift. Thank You for brave people like Martin Luther who told the truth about Your grace.
ask: Help us remember that we can’t earn Your love and don’t have to.

title: Here I Stand
verses: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
Therefore we will not fear though the earth gives way, though the mountains be moved into the heart of the sea,
though its waters roar and foam, though the mountains tremble at its swelling. Selah
The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah
story: After the 95 Theses, Luther kept writing books about the good news of Jesus. The pope and the church leaders were furious. They ordered Luther to take back everything he had written. Luther refused, so in 1521 he was called to a city named Worms to stand trial before the most powerful man in Europe, Emperor Charles V.

Luther’s friends were afraid. Years earlier, another preacher named Jan Hus had been promised safety at a trial like this, and he was burned at the stake anyway. But Luther said he would go even if there were as many devils in Worms as tiles on the roofs.

Luther walked into a great hall packed with princes, bishops, and soldiers. On a table sat a big pile of his books. An official pointed to them and asked two questions: “Did you write these books? And will you take back what is in them?” Luther said yes, they were his. Then, surprising everyone, he asked for a day to think and pray. That night, Luther prayed hard, asking God for courage.

The next day, the hall was even more crowded. Luther stood before the emperor and said: “Unless I am convinced by Scripture and plain reason, I cannot and will not take anything back. My conscience is captive to the Word of God. Here I stand. I can do no other. God help me. Amen.”

Luther was declared an outlaw. Anyone could capture him, or even kill him, without punishment. Luther left Worms not knowing what would happen to him. But he knew Who was with him. Years later he wrote a hymn based on tonight’s psalm: “A Mighty Fortress Is Our God.”
teach: Luther wasn’t brave because he was strong. He was brave because he trusted God’s Word more than any king. Psalm 46 says God is our refuge and fortress, a safe place to run when things are scary.
You won’t stand before an emperor, but you will have moments when standing for Jesus is hard. God is your fortress then too.
q: Who did Luther stand in front of? Who helped Luther be brave?
Why did Luther ask for one more day before he answered? What do you do when you need courage?
Luther said his conscience was “captive to the Word of God.” What does that mean? When might standing on God’s Word cost you something?
prayer: Mighty God, You are our refuge and strength. Thank You for giving Martin Luther courage to stand on Your Word, even when it was dangerous.
ask: When we are afraid, be our fortress, and help us stand for You.

kids.lede: Luther stood before the emperor and would not take back the truth about Jesus. God gave him courage!

title: The Knight in the Castle
verses: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
All Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness,
that the man of God may be complete, equipped for every good work.
story: Remember, Luther left Worms as an outlaw. As he rode home through a dark forest, a band of masked horsemen burst out of the trees. They grabbed Luther, threw him on a horse, and galloped away. News spread that Luther had been kidnapped, maybe even killed.

But it was a rescue! The horsemen were sent by Luther’s friend, Prince Frederick the Wise, to hide him where no one could find him. They took him to Wartburg Castle, high on a hill. To keep his secret, Luther grew a beard, wore a knight’s clothes, and went by a new name: Knight George.

Luther could have just waited it out. Instead, he got to work on something he had dreamed about for a long time. In those days, the Bible was mostly in Latin, a language ordinary people couldn’t read. Luther wanted every farmer, mother, and child in Germany to be able to read God’s Word for themselves.

So, alone in a small room by candlelight, Luther translated the whole New Testament from Greek into German. It took him only about eleven weeks! When it was printed, thousands of copies sold right away, and families read the Bible together at home in their own language for the first time. (There’s an old legend that Luther once threw his inkwell at the devil in that room. Nobody knows if it’s true, but people still show visitors an ink spot on the wall!)
The Bible you have on your shelf, in English, is there because people like Luther and other translators worked hard so that everyone could hear God speak in their own words.
teach: God’s Word is like a lamp in a dark forest. It doesn’t show us everything at once, but it lights up the next step.
2 Timothy says all Scripture is “breathed out by God.” When we read the Bible, God Himself is speaking to us. That’s why Luther thought every family needed one.
q: Where did Luther hide? What did he write in the castle?
Why couldn’t most people read the Bible before Luther? Why did Luther want families to read it at home?
What would change if you could never read the Bible yourself? How is God’s Word a lamp for the decisions you face?
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for Your Word, our lamp and light. Thank You for keeping Martin Luther safe, and for giving people the Bible in their own language.
ask: Help us love Your Word and read it together.

title: A Book for Every Family
reader: Mom or Dad, with everyone saying verse 7 together
verses: “Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one.
You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might.
And these words that I command you today shall be on your heart.
You shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise.
story_title: Luther’s family and the Small Catechism
story: When Luther came out of hiding, the Reformation was spreading everywhere. Some nuns who had read his writings wanted to leave their convent and serve God in ordinary life. Leaving was dangerous, so a friend of Luther’s smuggled twelve of them out in his wagon, hidden among barrels of fish!

One of those nuns was a strong, smart woman named Katharina von Bora. In 1525, she and Martin Luther got married. Their home in Wittenberg became noisy and full: six children, students, guests, and friends crowded around the dinner table. Katie ran the house, the farm, and even a brewery. Luther called her “my lord Katie.”

A few years later, Luther traveled around visiting churches, and he was shocked. Many people, and even some pastors, didn’t know the Lord’s Prayer, the Ten Commandments, or the Creed. Luther thought, “Who will teach the children?” And he decided the answer was: their parents.

So in 1529 Luther wrote the Small Catechism. It’s short and simple, with the Ten Commandments, the Creed, the Lord’s Prayer, Baptism, Confession, and the Lord’s Supper, each with the question, “What does this mean?” At the top of each part he wrote that it was for “the head of the family” to teach “to his household.” It was made for families to use at home, together.

Luther himself said that even as an old doctor of the church, he still prayed the catechism every day, like a child. Five hundred years later, families all over the world still use it. In fact, that’s exactly what our family is doing every night.
teach: Deuteronomy 6 says to talk about God’s Word “when you sit in your house.” Luther believed the most important church lessons happen at home, not just at church or school.
Every night we gather, read God’s Word, and pray, we’re doing exactly what God asked and what Luther hoped families would do.
q: How did Katie escape the convent? Who did Luther write the Small Catechism for?
What surprised Luther when he visited churches? Why do you think he wanted parents to be the teachers?
Why might faith learned at home stick better than faith learned only at church or school? What part of the catechism do you know best?
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for Martin and Katie Luther and their family, and for the Small Catechism that still teaches families today. Thank You for our family and for our time together every night.
ask: Write Your Word on our hearts, and keep our family close to You.

title: The Father Who Ran
verses: And he arose and came to his father. But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and felt compassion, and ran and embraced him and kissed him.
And the son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring quickly the best robe, and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet.
And bring the fattened calf and kill it, and let us eat and celebrate.
For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found.’ And they began to celebrate.
story: Jesus told a story about a father who had two sons. One day the younger son said, “Dad, I don’t want to wait until you die. Give me my share of your money now.” That was a terrible thing to say. It was like telling his father, “I wish you were already gone.” But the father divided up his money and gave the younger son his share.

The son packed up and moved to a faraway country. He spent every penny on parties and foolish living. Then a famine came, and he had nothing left. The only job he could find was feeding pigs, and he was so hungry he wished he could eat the pig food.

Finally he came to his senses. “My father’s servants have plenty of bread, and I’m starving! I’ll go home and say, ‘Father, I have sinned. I’m not good enough to be your son anymore. Just let me be one of your workers.’” So he started the long walk home, practicing his speech.

But while he was still far away, his father saw him. The father must have been watching the road every day. And he did something no proper man did in those days: he picked up his robe and ran. He threw his arms around his dirty, smelly son and kissed him. The son started his speech, but the father didn’t even let him finish. “Quick! Bring the best robe, a ring, and shoes! Let’s have a feast! My son was dead, and he’s alive again. He was lost, and now he’s found!”
teach: The son came home with a plan to earn his way back. The father didn’t want his plan. He just wanted his son. That’s grace: God’s love we don’t deserve and can’t earn.
Last week Luther discovered this same thing. Our Father in heaven runs to us in Jesus, and He welcomes us home every time we come back sorry.
q: What did the father do when he saw his son coming? What gifts did he give him?
What was the son planning to say? Why didn’t the father let him finish?
Why is it hard for people to believe God’s love is free? Is there anything that could make the Father stop watching the road for you?
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for running to us in Jesus. Thank You that we don’t have to earn our way back to You.
ask: When we wander away, bring us home, and help us welcome others the way You welcome us.

kids.lede: The lost son came home, and his father ran to hug him and threw a party! That’s how God loves us: by grace alone.
blanks: The younger son spent all his ___.

quiz: Did the son have to earn his way back?

title: Count the Stars
verses: And he brought him outside and said, “Look toward heaven, and number the stars, if you are able to number them.” Then he said to him, “So shall your offspring be.”
And he believed the LORD, and he counted it to him as righteousness.
story: A long time ago, God spoke to a man named Abram. (Later God changed his name to Abraham.) God said, “Leave your home and go to a land I will show you. I will make you into a great nation, and through you all the families of the earth will be blessed.” So Abram packed up his tents and animals and left, not knowing exactly where he was going.

But there was one big problem. Abram and his wife Sarai had no children, and they were getting old. How could Abram become a great nation without even one child? Years went by, and still no baby. Abram began to worry. “Lord,” he said, “You haven’t given me any children. Is a servant going to get everything when I die?”

So one night, God brought Abram outside his tent. “Look up at the sky,” God said. “Count the stars, if you can.” Abram looked up. There were no city lights back then, so the sky was packed with more stars than anyone could ever count. Then God said, “That’s how many children and grandchildren and great-grandchildren you will have.”

Abram was old. Nothing about it made sense. But the Bible says: “He believed the LORD, and He counted it to him as righteousness.” Abram didn’t do anything to earn it. He simply trusted God’s promise, and God counted him as right. Many years later, when Abraham was 100 years old, God kept His promise, and baby Isaac was born. And from Abraham’s family, Jesus Himself would one day come.
teach: Faith means trusting God’s promise, even when we can’t see how it will happen. Abraham didn’t become right with God by being good. He trusted, and God counted it as righteousness. Paul uses this exact verse in Romans 4 to teach that we are saved by faith.
And even our faith is God’s gift. He creates it through His Word, like a promise spoken under the stars.
q: What did God tell Abram to count? How many stars could he count?
Why was it hard for Abram to believe God’s promise? What did God count as righteousness?
Faith isn’t a feeling. It’s trusting a promise. What promise of God is hardest for you to trust right now?
prayer: Faithful God, thank You for keeping Your promise to Abraham and sending Jesus through his family. Thank You for giving us faith to trust You.
ask: When Your promises are hard to believe, strengthen our faith.

kids.lede: God told Abraham to count the stars. Abraham believed God’s promise, and God counted him righteous by faith alone!
blanks: God told Abram to count the ___.
quiz: Could Abram count all the stars?
kids.draw: Draw a night sky full of stars. Write a promise from God in the middle.
mv: “He believed the LORD, and he counted it to him as righteousness.”

title: It Is Written
verses: Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
And after fasting forty days and forty nights, he was hungry.
And the tempter came and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command these stones to become loaves of bread.”
But he answered, “It is written, “‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.’”
story: Right after Jesus was baptized in the Jordan River, the Holy Spirit led Him out into the wilderness: a hot, dry, rocky desert with no food and no people. Jesus stayed there forty days and forty nights without eating anything. You can imagine how hungry He was.

That’s when the devil came. He pointed at the stones on the ground. “If You are the Son of God, turn these stones into bread.” Jesus could have done it easily. But Jesus answered with God’s Word: “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.’”

So the devil tried again. He took Jesus to the very top of the temple. “Jump! The Bible says God’s angels will catch You.” The devil was even quoting Scripture, twisting it to trick Jesus. But Jesus answered, “It is also written, ‘You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.’”

One last time, the devil showed Jesus all the kingdoms of the world. “I’ll give You all of this, if You just bow down and worship me.” Jesus said, “Be gone, Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God and Him only shall you serve.’” And the devil left Him, and angels came and took care of Jesus.
Three times the devil attacked, and three times Jesus fought back with the same weapon: “It is written.”
teach: Jesus didn’t win with clever arguments or a feeling. He used God’s Word. That’s what Luther meant by Scripture alone: God’s Word is the final say, above any person, any king, or any trick of the devil.
Ephesians 6 calls God’s Word “the sword of the Spirit.” And notice where Jesus won: in the very place Adam and Eve, and all of us, have lost. He resisted for us.
q: What did the devil want Jesus to turn into bread? What did Jesus say every time?
Why do you think Jesus answered with Bible verses instead of His own words? What Bible verse do you know by heart?
The devil quoted Scripture too, but twisted it. How can we tell when someone is using the Bible the wrong way? What “stones into bread” temptations do you face?
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for standing strong against the devil for us. Thank You for Your Word, which is stronger than any temptation.
ask: Put Your Word in our hearts, so we can say “It is written” when we are tempted.

kids.lede: Three times the devil tried to trick Jesus, and three times Jesus answered, “It is written!” God’s Word is our final say.

title: Remember Me
verses: One of the criminals who were hanged railed at him, saying, “Are you not the Christ? Save yourself and us!”
But the other rebuked him, saying, “Do you not fear God, since you are under the same sentence of condemnation?
And we indeed justly, for we are receiving the due reward of our deeds; but this man has done nothing wrong.”
And he said, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.”
And he said to him, “Truly, I say to you, today you will be with me in paradise.”
story: On the day Jesus died, He wasn’t alone on the hill called Calvary. Two criminals were crucified with Him, one on His right and one on His left. They had done terrible things, and now they were being punished.
Crowds stood around making fun of Jesus. “He saved others! Let Him save Himself!” Even one of the criminals joined in, sneering, “Aren’t You the Christ? Save Yourself, and us too!”

But the other criminal spoke up. “Don’t you fear God? We deserve this. We’re getting what our actions earned. But this man hasn’t done anything wrong.” Then he turned his head toward Jesus and said, “Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom.”

Think about it: this man had no time left to fix his life. He couldn’t go to church, give money, or make up for what he’d done. His hands and feet were nailed down. All he could do was ask Jesus. And Jesus answered him with one of the most beautiful promises in the whole Bible: “Truly, I say to you, today you will be with Me in paradise.”
teach: The thief had nothing to offer but his need. Jesus was enough. We are saved by Christ alone: not by Jesus plus our good works, plus the saints, or plus anything else.
That’s the center of everything the Reformation was about. Grace, faith, and Scripture all point to one person: Jesus, who died for the thief and for us.
q: What did the second thief ask Jesus? Where did Jesus say he would go?
What could the thief do to earn heaven? Why did Jesus say yes to him anyway?
Some people say deathbed faith isn’t fair. Why does this story actually show how grace works? What does “Christ alone” rule out?
prayer: Lord Jesus, remember us, as You remembered the thief on the cross. Thank You for dying for us, and for being all we need.
ask: Help us trust You alone, and never think we have to add anything to what You did.

title: A Great Cloud of Witnesses
verses: Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight, and sin which clings so closely, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us,
looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is seated at the right hand of the throne of God.
story_title: Reformation Day and All Saints’ Day
story: Tomorrow, October 31, is Reformation Day, the day Luther nailed up his 95 Theses. And the very next day, November 1, is All Saints’ Day. Luther picked October 31 on purpose: the night before All Saints’, when lots of people would be at church.

Ten years after the 95 Theses, in 1527, a deadly disease called the plague came to Wittenberg. Most people who could leave, did. The university moved away. Luther’s prince ordered him to leave too. But Luther stayed. He said a pastor shouldn’t run away when his people needed him. Martin and Katie opened their home and cared for the sick, even while Katie was expecting a baby.

Some of the people they loved died that year. In those hard days, Luther wrote a hymn based on Psalm 46, the psalm we read last week: “A mighty fortress is our God, a trusty shield and weapon.” Its last verse says that even if they take our bodies, goods, honor, child, and spouse, “the kingdom ours remaineth.”

That’s what All Saints’ Day is about. In the church, a “saint” is any believer in Jesus. On All Saints’ we remember the Christians who have died in the faith: people from the Bible, people like Luther and Katie, and people we know and love. They aren’t gone. They’re with Jesus. Hebrews says they’re like a great crowd cheering us on in a race, as we keep running toward Jesus too.
teach: The saints who died in Christ are with Him now, and we’ll see them again at the resurrection. We don’t pray to them or talk to them, but we thank God for them and follow their faith.
Every time we receive the Lord’s Supper, we join “with angels and archangels and with all the company of heaven.” We’re all one family in Jesus.
q: What is a saint? Who are the saints cheering for?
Why did Luther stay in Wittenberg when the plague came? Who is someone we know who is with Jesus now?
Hebrews says to run with endurance, looking to Jesus. What does a runner have to lay aside to finish? What’s weighing you down in your race of faith?
prayer: Almighty God, thank You for Martin Luther and for all Your saints who have finished the race and now rest with Jesus. Thank You for the people we love who are with You now.
ask: Help us lay aside every weight and keep running, looking to Jesus, until we see them again.

title: The King Who Found the Book
verses: I have stored up your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you.
story: Long before Martin Luther, there was a reformation right in the Bible. Josiah became king of Judah when he was only eight years old. The kings before him had worshiped idols and forgotten God, and the temple in Jerusalem had fallen apart.

When Josiah grew up, he told workers to repair the temple. While they were cleaning, the high priest found something dusty in a back room: the Book of the Law, God’s Word that had been lost for years! They read it to the king. When Josiah heard it, he tore his robes. “We have not been doing what God says!”

Josiah gathered all the people, young and old, and read the whole book out loud to them. Then he promised to follow the Lord with all his heart. He tore down the idols, cleaned out the temple, and held the biggest Passover celebration in hundreds of years. God’s Word, found again, changed a whole nation, just like it did in Luther’s day.
teach: “Reformation” means being formed again around God’s Word. It happened with Josiah, it happened with Luther, and it happens in us every time we hear God’s Word and turn back to Him.
q: How old was Josiah when he became king? What did the workers find in the temple?
Why did Josiah tear his robes when he heard God’s Word?

prayer: Lord God, thank You for giving us Your Word, and for leaders like Josiah and Luther who helped people find it again.
ask: Help us store up Your Word in our hearts.

title: Lazarus, Come Out!
verses: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live,
and everyone who lives and believes in me shall never die. Do you believe this?”
story: Jesus had three dear friends: Mary, Martha, and their brother Lazarus. One day Lazarus got very sick, and the sisters sent word to Jesus. But by the time Jesus arrived, Lazarus had died and had been in the tomb for four days.

Martha ran to meet Jesus. “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.” Jesus told her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Me, though he die, yet shall he live.” Then Jesus went to the tomb, and He cried. Jesus loved His friend.

Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Then He prayed and shouted in a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!” And Lazarus walked out of the tomb, still wrapped in burial cloths! Jesus said, “Unbind him, and let him go.” Death had to obey Jesus.
teach: Today we remember Christians who have died and are now with Jesus. Death is real and it is sad. Jesus cried too. But it isn’t the end. The same voice that called Lazarus will call all believers out of their graves on the Last Day.
q: What did Jesus shout at the tomb? Why did Jesus cry?
What did Jesus tell Martha about who He is?
How does Jesus being “the resurrection and the life” change how Christians grieve?
prayer: Lord Jesus, You are the resurrection and the life. Thank You for all Your saints who now rest with You, and for the people we love who have died in the faith.
ask: Comfort everyone who is sad, and keep us in faith until we see them again.

title: God Made Everything
verses: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
And God saw everything that he had made, and behold, it was very good. And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.
story: In the very beginning, there was nothing at all: no sky, no ground, no people, not even light. Only God. Then God spoke. “Let there be light,” and there was light! On the first day God made day and night.

Day by day, God kept speaking, and everything He said happened. He made the sky and the waters. He made dry land with trees, flowers, and fruit. He hung the sun, the moon, and the stars. He filled the seas with fish and the sky with birds. He made animals of every kind: lions, ladybugs, elephants, and puppies.

On the sixth day, God did something special. He made a man, Adam, from the dust of the ground and breathed life into him. Then He made a woman, Eve. God made people in His own image, to know Him and love Him. God looked at everything He had made, and it was very good. On the seventh day, God rested.
teach: God made everything out of nothing, just by speaking. That means everything belongs to Him, including us. Luther’s explanation of the First Article says, “I believe that God has made me and all creatures.” You are not an accident. God made you on purpose.
q: What did God make on the first day? What is your favorite thing God made?
How did God make everything? What made people different from animals?
What does it mean that you were made in God’s image? How should that change how we treat other people?
prayer: Creator God, thank You for making the whole world and for making each of us. Everything You made is good.
ask: Help us take care of Your world and thank You for it.

title: The First Promise
verses: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring; he shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.”
story: God put Adam and Eve in a beautiful garden called Eden. They could eat from every tree except one: the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. “If you eat from that one,” God said, “you will die.”

One day the devil, disguised as a serpent, spoke to Eve. “Did God really say that? You won’t die. You’ll be like God!” Eve looked at the fruit. It looked so good. She ate some and gave some to Adam, and he ate too. Right away they felt ashamed and hid from God among the trees.

God came walking in the garden. “Where are you?” Adam blamed Eve, and Eve blamed the serpent. Sin had come into the world, and now there would be pain and death. But God, even then, made a promise. He told the serpent that one day a child of the woman would crush his head. That was the very first promise of Jesus, who would defeat the devil on the cross.
teach: Sin made Adam and Eve hide from God. Sin still makes us want to hide and blame others. But God didn’t leave them. He came looking for them and gave them a promise. God always comes looking for us too.
q: What did the serpent say to Eve? What did Adam and Eve do after they ate?
Who did Adam blame? Who did Eve blame? Why do we blame others when we do wrong?
Genesis 3:15 is called the “first Gospel.” How does it point to Jesus?
prayer: Lord God, we are sorry that we sin like Adam and Eve. Thank You for coming to look for us, and for sending Jesus to crush the devil.
ask: When we want to hide or blame, help us come to You and confess.

title: Noah and the Rainbow
verses: I have set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
story: After Adam and Eve, the world filled up with people, and they got worse and worse. Everyone did evil all the time. God was sad that He had made people. But one man, Noah, trusted God.

God told Noah, “Build a giant boat, an ark, because I am going to send a flood.” Noah obeyed, even though people probably laughed at him. When the ark was finished, God sent animals two by two, and Noah’s family went inside. Then God Himself shut the door. It rained forty days and forty nights until water covered even the mountains. But everyone inside the ark was safe.

After many months, the water went down. Noah sent out a dove, and it came back with an olive leaf. At last the ark rested on dry ground, and everyone came out. Noah thanked God, and God put a rainbow in the sky. “I will never again destroy the earth with a flood,” He promised. Every rainbow is God keeping His promise.
teach: The ark saved Noah’s family through the water. 1 Peter 3 says Baptism is like that: God saves us through water and puts us safe inside His Church. And every time you see a rainbow, God is reminding you that He keeps His promises.
q: How many of each animal went into the ark? Who shut the door?
Why do you think people laughed at Noah? Why did he keep building?
1 Peter 3:20–21 connects the flood with Baptism. How is Baptism like the ark?
prayer: Faithful God, thank You for keeping Noah safe in the ark, and for keeping us safe in Your family through Baptism.
ask: When we see a rainbow, help us remember that You always keep Your promises.

title: The Tower of Babel
verses: Prov 16:18
Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
James 4:10
Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you.
story: After the flood, Noah’s family grew into many families, and they all spoke one language. They settled on a flat plain and had an idea. “Let’s make bricks and build a city with a tower that reaches up to heaven. Then we’ll make a great name for ourselves!”

They didn’t want to give glory to God. They wanted glory for themselves. So they baked bricks and stacked them higher and higher. But God came down to see their tower. He said, “If they do this, nothing will stop them from doing whatever proud thing they want.”

So God mixed up their language. Suddenly one person said “Pass the bricks,” and the other heard nonsense! Nobody could understand anyone. They had to stop building, and they spread out over the whole earth. The city was called Babel, because there God confused their language.
teach: Pride says, “Look at me.” Faith says, “Look at God.” Many years later, on Pentecost, God did the opposite of Babel: the apostles spoke and everyone heard the good news of Jesus in their own language. God brings people back together in Jesus.
q: What were the people building? What did God do to their language?
Why did the people want to build the tower? What does it mean to be proud?
How is Pentecost (Acts 2) like Babel turned upside down? Where do you see people trying to “make a name” for themselves?
prayer: Heavenly Father, forgive us when we are proud and want glory for ourselves. Thank You for Jesus, who humbled Himself for us.
ask: Teach us to give You the glory in everything we do.

title: God Will Provide
verses: Abraham said, “God will provide for himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So they went both of them together.
story: Remember Abraham, who counted the stars? God finally gave him and Sarah a son, Isaac, the promised child. Abraham loved him very much. Then one day God tested Abraham. “Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and offer him as a sacrifice on a mountain I will show you.”

Abraham’s heart must have been breaking, but he trusted God. He got up early, and he and Isaac climbed the mountain. Isaac carried the wood on his back. “Father,” Isaac said, “here is the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb?” Abraham answered, “God will provide the lamb, my son.”

At the top, Abraham built an altar and laid Isaac on it. But just then the angel of the Lord called out, “Abraham! Don’t hurt the boy! Now I know you trust God.” Abraham looked up, and there was a ram caught by its horns in a bush. God had provided! Abraham named the place “The Lord Will Provide.”
teach: This story points straight to Jesus. Isaac carried wood up a mountain; Jesus carried a wooden cross up a hill. God spared Isaac, but He did not spare His own Son. Jesus is the Lamb God provided for us, as John the Baptist said: “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!”
q: What did Isaac carry up the mountain? What did God provide instead of Isaac?
Why do you think God tested Abraham? How did Abraham show he trusted God?
List the ways Isaac’s story looks like Jesus’ story. Where is the big difference?
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for providing the ram for Abraham, and for providing Jesus, the Lamb of God, for us.
ask: When we can’t see how things will work out, help us trust that You will provide.

kids.lede: God tested Abraham, and then provided a ram instead of Isaac. God provided Jesus, the Lamb, for us!
blanks: God sent a ___ caught in a bush.
quiz: Did God let Abraham hurt Isaac?
Who is the Lamb God provided for us?
kids.draw: Draw the ram caught in the bush.
mv: “God will provide for himself the lamb.”

title: Jacob’s Ladder
verses: Behold, I am with you and will keep you wherever you go, and will bring you back to this land. For I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.”
story: Isaac grew up and had twin sons, Esau and Jacob. Jacob tricked his brother and his father to get the family blessing, and Esau was so angry that Jacob had to run away from home. He ran far into the wilderness, all alone.

That night, Jacob used a stone for a pillow and fell asleep. He had an amazing dream: a stairway reaching from the ground all the way up to heaven, with God’s angels going up and down on it. And at the top stood the Lord Himself.

God said, “I am the God of Abraham and Isaac. I will give you this land and many children, and through your family all the earth will be blessed. I am with you and will keep you wherever you go.” Jacob woke up and said, “Surely the Lord is in this place, and I did not know it!” God made that promise to a runaway who didn’t deserve it.
teach: Jacob had messed up badly, and he was alone and afraid. God didn’t come to scold him. He came with a promise. Jesus later said He Himself is the ladder (John 1:51): He connects heaven and earth, and brings God to us.
q: What did Jacob use for a pillow? What was on the stairway?
Why was Jacob running away? Did he deserve God’s promise?
Jesus said He is like Jacob’s ladder (John 1:51). What did He mean?
prayer: Lord God, thank You for being with Jacob even when he ran away, and for being with us wherever we go.
ask: When we feel alone, remind us that You are with us.

blanks: Jacob used a ___ for a pillow.
He dreamed of a ___ to heaven.
kids.draw: Draw Jacob’s stairway with angels on it.
mv: “I am with you and will keep you wherever you go.”

title: How Majestic Is Your Name
verses: O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth! You have set your glory above the heavens.
When I look at your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars, which you have set in place,
what is man that you are mindful of him, and the son of man that you care for him?
story: Many years later, a shepherd boy named David spent long nights in the fields watching his sheep. With no lights anywhere, the sky above him was full of stars. David looked up and thought about how huge God must be to make all that.

Then he thought about how small he was. “When I look at the heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars… who am I that You even think about me?” But God doesn’t just think about us. He cares for us. He crowned people with glory and gave them His creation to take care of.

David wrote his thoughts into a song, Psalm 8. Thousands of years later, we still sing it. And one day, Jesus quoted this psalm when children shouted “Hosanna!” to Him in the temple: “Out of the mouth of babies and infants, you have prepared praise.” God loves to hear even little children praise Him.
teach: God made billions of stars, and He knows every one by name. And He knows your name too. That’s the wonder of Psalm 8: the God who made everything cares about you.
q: Who wrote Psalm 8? What did he see in the sky?
How does looking at the stars make you feel? Why would God care about people?
Jesus quoted Psalm 8 when children praised Him (Matthew 21:16). Why do you think God loves the praise of children?
prayer: O Lord our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth! Thank You for making the stars, and for caring about each of us.
ask: Help us praise You with our whole lives.

kids.lede: David looked at the stars and sang, “How majestic is Your name!” The God who made the stars cares about you!
blanks: He looked at the moon and the ___.
kids.draw: Go outside tonight and look at the stars. Then draw what you see.
mv: “O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth!”

title: The Coat of Many Colors
verses: Now Israel loved Joseph more than any other of his sons, because he was the son of his old age. And he made him a robe of many colors.
story: Jacob, who was also called Israel, had twelve sons. His favorite was Joseph, and he didn’t hide it. He gave Joseph a beautiful robe of many colors, and the other brothers didn’t get one. That made them jealous.

Then Joseph had two dreams. In one, his brothers’ bundles of grain bowed down to his bundle. In the other, the sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to him. Joseph told his whole family about it. His brothers were furious. “Do you think you’re going to rule over us?”

The brothers hated Joseph so much they couldn’t even say a kind word to him. A family that should have loved each other was full of jealousy. But God had plans for Joseph’s dreams that no one could imagine yet.
teach: Jacob made a mistake by playing favorites, and Joseph made it worse by bragging. But the brothers chose to hate. Jealousy grows when we compare ourselves to others. God gives each of us different gifts, and He loves every one of His children completely.
q: What special gift did Jacob give Joseph? What bowed down in Joseph’s dreams?
Why were the brothers jealous? Have you ever felt jealous of a brother or sister?
Who did wrong in this story? How does jealousy grow in a family, and how can it stop?
prayer: Heavenly Father, forgive us when we are jealous of others. Thank You for loving each of us completely.
ask: Help our family celebrate each other instead of comparing.

title: Sold!
verses: But when his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, they hated him and could not speak peacefully to him.
story: One day Jacob sent Joseph to check on his brothers, who were far away taking care of the sheep. When they saw him coming in his colorful robe, they said, “Here comes the dreamer! Let’s kill him and see what becomes of his dreams.”

Reuben, the oldest, convinced them not to kill him, so they tore off Joseph’s robe and threw him into an empty pit. Joseph cried for help, but they sat down to eat. Then a caravan of traders came by on the way to Egypt. Judah said, “Let’s sell him!” They sold their own brother for twenty pieces of silver.

The brothers dipped Joseph’s robe in goat’s blood and showed it to their father. Jacob thought a wild animal had killed Joseph, and he cried for days. Meanwhile, Joseph was carried off to Egypt as a slave. It looked like the worst thing that could happen. But God was still with Joseph.
teach: Joseph was betrayed by his own family. Jesus was betrayed too, for thirty pieces of silver. In both stories, what looked like the end was really the start of God’s rescue plan.
q: Where did the brothers throw Joseph? How much did they sell him for?
How do you think Joseph felt in the pit? How did Jacob feel?
Compare Joseph being sold with Jesus being betrayed by Judas. What’s similar?
prayer: Lord God, You were with Joseph in the pit and on the road to Egypt. Thank You that You never leave us, even when people hurt us.
ask: When we feel betrayed or alone, help us trust that You are still working.

kids.lede: Joseph’s brothers threw him in a pit and sold him as a slave. But God was still with him!

title: The Lord Was with Joseph
verses: The LORD was with Joseph, and he became a successful man, and he was in the house of his Egyptian master.
But the LORD was with Joseph and showed him steadfast love and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
story: In Egypt, Joseph was sold to a man named Potiphar, the captain of Pharaoh’s guard. Joseph worked hard and honestly, and the Bible says, “The Lord was with Joseph.” Everything he did went well, so Potiphar put him in charge of his whole house.

But Potiphar’s wife lied about Joseph and said he had done something bad. Even though Joseph did nothing wrong, Potiphar threw him in prison. Again, Joseph could have given up. But the Bible says it again: “The Lord was with Joseph.” Soon the jailer put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners.

Two prisoners, Pharaoh’s cupbearer and baker, had strange dreams. God helped Joseph explain them: the cupbearer would get his job back in three days. “Please remember me when you get out!” Joseph said. It happened just as Joseph said. But the cupbearer forgot all about Joseph, and Joseph stayed in prison two more years.
teach: Joseph was a slave and then a prisoner for something he didn’t do. Yet he stayed honest and kept working hard. Twice the Bible says, “The Lord was with Joseph.” God doesn’t always take us out of hard places, but He is always with us in them.
q: Who bought Joseph? Where did Joseph go after someone lied about him?
How many times does today’s reading say “The LORD was with Joseph”? Why does that matter?
Joseph was faithful even when life was unfair. What does faithfulness look like when you’re treated unfairly?
prayer: Lord God, You were with Joseph as a slave and in prison. Thank You for being with us in every hard place.
ask: Help us be honest and faithful even when life feels unfair.

kids.lede: Joseph ended up in prison for something he didn’t do. But the Lord was with Joseph!
blanks: Joseph worked for a man named ___.
quiz: Who was with Joseph in prison?
kids.draw: Draw Joseph helping in the prison.

title: Pharaoh’s Dreams
verses: Joseph answered Pharaoh, “It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh a favorable answer.”
story: Two years later, Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, had two dreams that scared him. In the first, seven fat cows came up out of the Nile River, and then seven skinny, ugly cows came and ate them up! In the second, seven full heads of grain were swallowed by seven thin, dried-up ones. None of Pharaoh’s wise men could explain them.

Suddenly the cupbearer remembered. “There’s a young man in prison who explained my dream!” Pharaoh sent for Joseph right away. They shaved him, gave him new clothes, and brought him before the king. “I hear you can explain dreams,” said Pharaoh. Joseph answered, “It is not in me. God will give the answer.”

Joseph explained: “There will be seven years of plenty, then seven years of terrible famine. Pharaoh should choose a wise man to store up food during the good years.” Pharaoh said, “Who could be wiser than you?” He put his ring on Joseph’s finger and made him ruler over all Egypt, second only to Pharaoh himself. In one day, Joseph went from prisoner to prince.
teach: Joseph could have taken the credit. Instead he pointed to God. That humility is a gift. And God’s timing was perfect: if the cupbearer had remembered sooner, Joseph might have been freed and gone home, and wouldn’t have been there for this moment.
q: What ate the fat cows in Pharaoh’s dream? What job did Pharaoh give Joseph?
Joseph said, “It is not in me.” Who did he give credit to? Why is that important?
The cupbearer forgot Joseph for two years. How did God use even that delay?
prayer: Wise and powerful God, thank You for lifting Joseph up at just the right time. Your timing is always good.
ask: Help us give You the credit for every good thing, and trust Your timing.

title: The Brothers Come to Egypt
verses: Now therefore, please let your servant remain instead of the boy as a servant to my lord, and let the boy go back with his brothers.
story: Just as God said, the famine came. There was no food anywhere, except in Egypt, where Joseph had stored up grain. Back home, Jacob sent ten of Joseph’s brothers to Egypt to buy food, but he kept Benjamin, the youngest, at home. The brothers bowed down before the ruler of Egypt. They didn’t recognize him, but Joseph recognized them. His dream had come true! Joseph spoke roughly to them and said, “Next time, bring your youngest brother, or don’t come back.”

When the food ran out, the brothers had to go back, and this time Benjamin came too. Joseph wanted to know if his brothers had changed. So he tested them. He secretly put his silver cup in the sack of Benjamin, Jacob’s new favorite. Then he had the brothers arrested. “The one who had my cup will be my slave. The rest of you go home.”

Years before, the brothers had sold Joseph without a second thought. But now Judah stepped forward. “Please, my lord, let me stay as your slave instead of the boy. If he doesn’t come home, it will kill our father.” Judah, who once said, “Let’s sell him,” now offered his own life to save his brother. They really had changed.
teach: Judah offered to take Benjamin’s punishment. Many years later, Jesus, born from Judah’s family, did that for all of us. He took our place and our punishment on the cross.
q: Why did the brothers go to Egypt? What did Joseph hide in Benjamin’s sack?
Why did Joseph test his brothers? How did Judah show he had changed?
Judah offered to take Benjamin’s place. How is that a picture of what Jesus did?
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for taking our place and our punishment. Thank You for changing hearts, even the hardest ones.
ask: Help us love our brothers and sisters enough to stand up for them.

title: I Am Joseph
verses: So Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.” And they came near. And he said, “I am your brother, Joseph, whom you sold into Egypt.
And now do not be distressed or angry with yourselves because you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
story: When Joseph heard Judah offer to take Benjamin’s place, he couldn’t hold it in any longer. He sent all his servants out of the room and began to cry so loudly that people in the palace heard him. Then he said, “I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?”

His brothers were terrified. They couldn’t say a word. This was the brother they had sold! But Joseph said, “Come close. Don’t be upset with yourselves for selling me. God sent me here ahead of you to save lives.” Then he hugged Benjamin and cried, and he kissed all his brothers.

Joseph sent wagons to bring his father Jacob to Egypt. When Jacob heard “Joseph is alive and ruling Egypt,” he could hardly believe it. At last, father and son met again. Joseph threw his arms around his dad and cried for a long time. The family that had been broken was together again.
teach: Joseph had every reason to get revenge. He had the power to do it. Instead, he forgave. That kind of forgiveness only comes from knowing how much God has forgiven us. In Jesus, God doesn’t pay us back for our sins. He welcomes us close.
q: What did Joseph say to his brothers? How did they feel?
Joseph could have punished his brothers. Why did he forgive them?
Joseph saw God’s hand in his whole hard story. How can believing God is at work help us forgive someone?
prayer: Merciful Father, thank You that You forgive us and call us close instead of paying us back. Thank You for bringing Joseph’s family back together.
ask: Help us forgive each other the way You forgive us.

title: God Meant It for Good
verses: As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring it about that many people should be kept alive, as they are today.
story: Jacob’s family lived in Egypt for many years, safe from the famine. Jacob grew very old, blessed his sons and grandsons, and died. After the funeral, Joseph’s brothers got nervous. “What if Joseph was only being nice because of Dad? Now he might pay us back for everything.”

They sent Joseph a message: “Please forgive us.” Then they came and bowed down. “We are your servants.” Joseph cried again. “Don’t be afraid. Am I in the place of God? You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to save many lives.”

Joseph looked back over his whole life: the jealous brothers, the pit, slavery, the lie, prison, the forgotten promise. All of it had been painful. But God had been weaving every piece into a plan to save people. Joseph comforted his brothers and promised to take care of them and their children.
teach: Romans 8:28 says, “For those who love God all things work together for good.” That doesn’t mean bad things are good. It means God is bigger than the bad things. The greatest example is the cross: the worst thing people ever did, God used to save the world.
q: What were the brothers afraid of? What did Joseph tell them?
Name the hard things that happened to Joseph. How did God use them?
“You meant evil, but God meant it for good.” How is the cross the biggest example of this?
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for working in every part of our lives, even the hard parts. Thank You for the cross, where You turned the worst evil into our salvation.
ask: Help us trust You when we can’t see what You are doing.

title: The Baby in the Basket
verses: When the child grew older, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, “Because,” she said, “I drew him out of the water.”
story: Many years after Joseph, Jacob’s family had grown into a huge nation called Israel. A new Pharaoh came who didn’t remember Joseph. He was afraid of the Israelites, so he made them slaves. Then he gave a terrible order: every baby boy born to the Israelites must be thrown into the Nile River.

One Israelite mother had a baby boy, and she hid him for three months. When she couldn’t hide him anymore, she made a little basket, covered it with tar so it would float, put her baby inside, and set it among the reeds by the river. His big sister Miriam watched to see what would happen.

Pharaoh’s own daughter came down to the river to bathe. She saw the basket and opened it. The baby was crying, and she felt sorry for him. Miriam bravely ran up: “Should I find a Hebrew woman to take care of him for you?” She ran and got the baby’s own mother! The princess named him Moses, and God kept him safe for a big job ahead.
teach: Pharaoh wanted to destroy God’s people, but God used a basket, a brave big sister, and even Pharaoh’s own daughter to protect baby Moses. Nothing can stop God’s plans.
q: Where did Moses’ mother put him? Who watched over the basket?
How was Miriam brave? Who did she bring to take care of Moses?
Pharaoh’s order was meant to destroy Israel. How did God turn it around?
prayer: Lord God, thank You for protecting baby Moses, and for protecting us. Thank You for brave big sisters and brothers.
ask: Help us be brave to help others, like Miriam.

kids.lede: Moses’ mother put him in a basket in the river. Pharaoh’s daughter found him, and God kept him safe!
blanks: Moses’ mother put him in a ___.
quiz: Who found the baby in the basket?
kids.draw: Draw baby Moses in his basket in the reeds.
mv: “I drew him out of the water.”

title: The Burning Bush
verses: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM.” And he said, “Say this to the people of Israel: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
story: Moses grew up in Pharaoh’s palace, but he knew he was an Israelite. One day he saw an Egyptian beating an Israelite slave, and in anger Moses killed the Egyptian. Pharaoh found out, and Moses ran far away into the desert. For forty years he lived there as a shepherd.

One day, while watching his sheep near a mountain, Moses saw something strange: a bush on fire, but it wasn’t burning up! As he walked closer, God called from the bush, “Moses, Moses! Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.”

God said, “I have seen My people suffering in Egypt. I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring them out.” Moses was scared. “Who am I to do that? And what’s Your name, if they ask?” God answered, “I AM WHO I AM.” God always was, always is, and always will be. Moses still made excuses, but God promised, “I will be with you.”
teach: God’s name, “I AM,” means He doesn’t depend on anything. He has no beginning and no end. Later Jesus said, “Before Abraham was, I am,” telling everyone He is God. The great I AM was with Moses, and He is with us.
q: What was strange about the bush? Why did Moses take off his sandals?
What excuses did Moses make? What did God promise him?
Jesus used the name “I am” about Himself (John 8:58). What was He saying?
prayer: Holy God, You are the great I AM. Thank You for calling Moses even after his mistakes, and for calling us too.
ask: When we feel too small for what You ask, remind us that You are with us.

kids.lede: God spoke to Moses from a bush that burned but didn’t burn up! God’s name is I AM.
blanks: Moses took care of ___ in the desert.
The bush was on ___ but didn’t burn up.
quiz: What did God send Moses to do?
kids.draw: Draw the burning bush and Moses taking off his sandals.

title: Let My People Go
verses: Afterward Moses and Aaron went and said to Pharaoh, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, ‘Let my people go, that they may hold a feast to me in the wilderness.’”
But Pharaoh said, “Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice and let Israel go? I do not know the LORD, and moreover, I will not let Israel go.”
story: Moses and his brother Aaron went to Pharaoh with God’s message: “Let My people go!” But Pharaoh refused. “Who is the Lord? I don’t know Him, and I won’t let Israel go.” Instead, he made the slaves work even harder.

So God sent plagues on Egypt. The Nile River turned to blood. Frogs hopped everywhere: in beds, in ovens, in bowls. Then came gnats, flies, sick animals, painful sores, giant hailstorms, and swarms of locusts that ate every green plant. Then thick darkness covered Egypt for three days, but the Israelites had light where they lived.

Each time, Pharaoh promised to let the people go. And each time, as soon as the plague stopped, he changed his mind and hardened his heart. Pharaoh found out who the Lord was: the one true God, stronger than all the gods of Egypt. But he still wouldn’t listen.
teach: Pharaoh kept saying no to God, again and again, until his heart became hard. When God speaks to us through His Word, the best thing we can do is listen right away. A soft heart says, “Yes, Lord.”
q: What did Moses tell Pharaoh? Name as many plagues as you can.
Why do you think Pharaoh kept changing his mind?
What does it mean to have a hard heart? How does God soften hearts?
prayer: Mighty God, You are stronger than every power in the world. Thank You for hearing Your people’s cries.
ask: Give us soft hearts that listen to Your Word and say yes to You.

kids.lede: Pharaoh wouldn’t let God’s people go, so God sent plagues. Pharaoh learned who the Lord is!
quiz: Did Pharaoh listen the first time?
Who is stronger than Egypt’s gods?
kids.draw: Draw your favorite plague. (Frogs are fun!)

title: The Passover
verses: The blood shall be a sign for you, on the houses where you are. And when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague will befall you to destroy you, when I strike the land of Egypt.
story: God told Moses there would be one last plague, the worst of all: the firstborn son in every house in Egypt would die. But God gave His people a way to be safe. Each family was to take a perfect lamb, sacrifice it, and paint its blood on the doorposts of their house.

That night, the families ate the lamb with bread made without yeast, because there was no time for the bread to rise. They ate with their sandals on and their walking sticks in their hands, ready to leave. At midnight, the Lord went through Egypt. But wherever He saw the blood on the door, He passed over that house.

A great cry went up in Egypt, even in Pharaoh’s palace. Finally Pharaoh called Moses in the night: “Go! Take your people and go!” After 430 years, Israel walked out of Egypt free. God told them to remember that night every year with a feast called the Passover.
teach: The blood of the lamb saved God’s people from death. Jesus is our Passover Lamb (1 Corinthians 5:7). His blood covers us, so death passes over us. And on the night before He died, Jesus celebrated the Passover with His disciples and gave us the Lord’s Supper.
q: What did the families paint on their doors? What did God do when He saw it?
Why did they eat with their sandals on and bread with no yeast?
Jesus is called our Passover Lamb. How does Passover help us understand the cross and the Lord’s Supper?
prayer: Lord Jesus, You are our Passover Lamb. Thank You for covering us with Your blood so that death passes over us.
ask: Thank You for the Lord’s Supper, where You give us Your body and blood for the forgiveness of sins.

kids.lede: God’s people painted lamb’s blood on their doors, and the Lord passed over them. Jesus is our Passover Lamb!
blanks: The Lord ___ over the houses with blood.
kids.draw: Draw a house with blood on the doorposts, and a family inside eating.
mv: “When I see the blood, I will pass over you.”

title: Through the Sea
verses: And Moses said to the people, “Fear not, stand firm, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will work for you today. For the Egyptians whom you see today, you shall never see again.
The LORD will fight for you, and you have only to be silent.”
story: God led His people out of Egypt with a pillar of cloud during the day and a pillar of fire at night. But soon Pharaoh changed his mind again. “What have we done? We let our slaves go!” He chased after them with six hundred chariots.

The Israelites were trapped: the sea in front of them and Pharaoh’s army behind them. They panicked. “Did you bring us out here to die?” But Moses said, “Don’t be afraid. Stand still and see how the Lord will save you. The Lord will fight for you.”

God told Moses to stretch out his staff over the sea. A strong wind blew all night, and the water split in two, with walls of water on the right and on the left! The people walked through on dry ground. When the Egyptians followed, the water came crashing back. Israel was safe on the other side, and Miriam led everyone in a song of praise.
teach: The people couldn’t save themselves. They could only watch God save them. That’s what salvation is: God does the work. Christians have always seen the Red Sea as a picture of Baptism, where God brings us through water from slavery to freedom.
q: What was in front of the Israelites? What was behind them?
Moses said, “The Lord will fight for you.” What did the people have to do?
How is crossing the Red Sea like Baptism (1 Corinthians 10:1–2)?
prayer: Lord God, You fought for Israel at the Red Sea, and You fought for us at the cross. Thank You for saving us when we couldn’t save ourselves.
ask: When we feel trapped, help us stand still and trust You.

kids.lede: God split the Red Sea so His people could walk through on dry ground!
blanks: Moses said, “The Lord will ___ for you.”
quiz: Did the people have to fight the Egyptians?
kids.draw: Draw the walls of water with God’s people walking through.

title: Bread from Heaven
verses: Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me shall not hunger, and whoever believes in me shall never thirst.
story: After crossing the sea, God’s people traveled into the desert. Soon they were hungry, and they started complaining. “We had plenty of food in Egypt! You brought us here to starve!” They forgot all the amazing things God had just done.

But God was patient. He said, “I will rain bread from heaven for you.” The next morning, the ground was covered with little white flakes that tasted like wafers made with honey. The people asked, “What is it?” In Hebrew that is “manna,” and that became its name. God also sent quail for meat in the evening.

Every morning, each family gathered just enough for that day. If they tried to save extra, it got wormy and smelly! But on the sixth day, they gathered twice as much, so they could rest on the Sabbath. For forty years in the desert, God fed His people every single day.
teach: God gave manna one day at a time, so the people would learn to trust Him every day. That’s why Jesus taught us to pray, “Give us this day our daily bread.” And Jesus Himself is the true bread from heaven, who gives eternal life.
q: What did God send from heaven? What did the people call it?
Why couldn’t they save extra manna? What was God teaching them?
Jesus said, “I am the bread of life.” What does He mean? How do we “eat” this bread?
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for feeding Your people in the desert, and for giving us our daily bread. Thank You for Jesus, the bread of life.
ask: When we complain, forgive us, and teach us to trust You day by day.

kids.lede: God rained manna from heaven every morning to feed His people. Jesus is the bread of life!
quiz: Who is the bread of life?
kids.draw: Draw the ground covered with manna, and people gathering it.

title: The Ten Commandments
verses: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
“You shall have no other gods before me.
story: Three months after leaving Egypt, God’s people came to a mountain called Sinai. Thunder rumbled, lightning flashed, and a thick cloud covered the mountain. A trumpet blast grew louder and louder, and the whole mountain shook. The people trembled.

God called Moses up the mountain, and there God gave His Ten Commandments, written on two stone tablets by God’s own finger. But notice how God began: “I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of slavery.” God rescued His people first, and then He gave them His commandments.

The commandments teach us how to love God (the first three) and how to love our neighbor (the other seven). They show us God’s good will. They also show us our sin, because no one keeps them perfectly. Only Jesus did. He kept every commandment for us, and then died for all the times we break them.
teach: God doesn’t say, “Obey Me and then I’ll save you.” He says, “I saved you, so now live as My people.” That’s why Luther explains every commandment in the Small Catechism starting with, “We should fear and love God.” We obey out of love for the God who rescued us.
q: Where did God give the Ten Commandments? What were they written on?
What did God say before He gave the commandments? Why does that order matter?
The Law shows us our sin. How does that make us need Jesus? Which commandment is hardest for you?
prayer: Holy God, thank You for rescuing us and for giving us Your good commandments. Forgive us for breaking them, and thank You for Jesus, who kept them all for us.
ask: Help us fear, love, and trust You above all things, and love our neighbor.

kids.lede: God gave His Ten Commandments on Mount Sinai, written on stone tablets with His own finger!
blanks: God gave the commandments on Mount ___.
They were written on two stone ___.
The first commandment: You shall have no other ___.
quiz: Did God rescue His people before giving the commandments?
Who kept all the commandments perfectly?
kids.draw: Draw the two stone tablets. Can you write the numbers 1 to 10 on them?
mv: “You shall have no other gods before me.”

title: The Walls of Jericho
verses: Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be frightened, and do not be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.”
story: After forty years in the desert, Moses died, and God chose Joshua to lead His people into the promised land. God told him, “Be strong and courageous. I will be with you wherever you go.” But the first city in their way was Jericho, with huge, thick walls and locked gates.

God gave Joshua a strange battle plan. “March around the city once a day for six days, with seven priests blowing trumpets in front of the ark. Don’t say a word. On the seventh day, march around seven times. Then the priests will blow a long blast, all the people will shout, and the walls will fall down.”

It sounded silly. Who wins a battle by walking? But Joshua and the people obeyed exactly. On the seventh day, after the seventh lap, the trumpets blasted, everyone shouted, and the great walls of Jericho came tumbling down flat! God won the battle, just as He promised.
teach: God’s plan didn’t make sense to human eyes, but God was the one fighting. He often works through things that look weak or silly, like water in Baptism, bread and wine in the Lord’s Supper, and words read from a book. That’s where His power is.
q: How many days did they march? What happened when they shouted?
Why do you think God gave such a strange plan?
God works through “ordinary” things like water, bread, and words. Why do you think He does that?
prayer: Mighty God, thank You for fighting for Your people at Jericho and for being with us wherever we go.
ask: Make us strong and courageous, trusting Your way even when it seems strange.
