title: Gideon’s Tiny Army
verses: And the angel of the LORD appeared to him and said to him, “The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor.”
story: Later, enemies called the Midianites kept stealing all of Israel’s food. A young man named Gideon was hiding in a winepress, secretly threshing wheat, when an angel appeared and said, “The Lord is with you, mighty warrior!” Gideon looked around. Mighty warrior? Him? “I’m the weakest one in my family!”

But God said, “I will be with you.” Gideon gathered 32,000 soldiers. God said, “Too many! If you win, you’ll think you did it yourselves.” He sent home everyone who was afraid, then had the rest drink from a stream and kept only the 300 who lapped water with their hands. 300 men against an army as thick as locusts!

In the middle of the night, the 300 surrounded the enemy camp. Each man had a trumpet and a torch hidden inside a clay jar. At Gideon’s signal, they blew their trumpets, smashed their jars so the torches blazed, and shouted, “A sword for the Lord and for Gideon!” The enemy panicked, and the whole army ran away.
teach: God kept making Gideon’s army smaller so everyone would know the victory came from God. Paul says God’s “power is made perfect in weakness” (2 Corinthians 12:9). When we feel small, we’re in a good spot for God to work.
q: Where was Gideon hiding? What did the 300 men carry?
Why did God make the army smaller and smaller?
God called fearful Gideon a “mighty man.” What does that tell you about how God sees you?
prayer: Lord God, thank You for using weak and small people to do Your work, so that You get the glory.
ask: When we feel too small or scared, remind us that You are with us.

kids.lede: God used Gideon and only 300 men with trumpets, jars, and torches to win the battle!
blanks: The angel called him a mighty ___.
God made the army smaller, down to ___.
quiz: Did Gideon feel strong at first?
Why did God use only 300 men?
kids.draw: Draw a clay jar with a torch inside, and a trumpet.
mv: “The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor.”

title: The One Who Came Back
verses: Then one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, praising God with a loud voice;
and he fell on his face at Jesus’ feet, giving him thanks. Now he was a Samaritan.
story: One day, as Jesus walked into a village, ten men stood far away and called out to Him. They had a terrible skin disease called leprosy. Because people were afraid of catching it, they had to live outside town, away from their families. “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”

Jesus said, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” That’s what you did after you got better. And as the ten men walked away, they looked down at their skin and saw they were healed! All ten were clean and healthy.

Nine of them kept going, probably running home to their families. But one man stopped, turned around, and ran back to Jesus, shouting praise to God. He fell at Jesus’ feet and said thank you. He was a Samaritan, a foreigner. Jesus asked, “Weren’t ten healed? Where are the other nine?” Then He told the man, “Get up. Your faith has made you well.”
teach: All ten were healed, but only one came back to say thank you. Tomorrow is Thanksgiving. God gives us so much every single day: food, family, home, and most of all Jesus. Saying thank you to God is a joyful way to live.
q: How many men were healed? How many came back to say thank you?
Why do you think the other nine didn’t come back?
Luther’s explanation of the First Article ends, “For all this it is my duty to thank and praise, serve and obey Him.” What are you most thankful for this year?
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for all the ways You heal and help us. Forgive us for the times we forget to say thank you.
ask: Give us thankful hearts tomorrow and every day.

kids.lede: Jesus healed ten sick men, but only one came back to say thank you!
blanks: Only one came back to say ___ you.
quiz: Who should we thank for good gifts?
kids.draw: Make a list or drawing of ten things you are thankful for.
mv: “…turned back, praising God with a loud voice.”

title: Enter His Gates with Thanksgiving
verses: Enter his gates with thanksgiving, and his courts with praise! Give thanks to him; bless his name!
For the LORD is good; his steadfast love endures forever, and his faithfulness to all generations.
story: In 1620, a group of Christians called the Pilgrims sailed across the stormy Atlantic Ocean on a small ship called the Mayflower. They wanted a place where they could worship God freely. The trip took more than two months, and when they landed, winter was already coming.

That first winter was terrible. They didn’t have enough food or warm houses, and about half of them died. In the spring, a Native American man named Squanto, who spoke English, helped them. He taught them how to plant corn, where to fish, and how to survive in their new home.

In the fall of 1621, the harvest came in. The Pilgrims had food for the winter! They held a feast for three days with their Wampanoag neighbors, and they thanked God for His care. Even after a year of so much loss, they knew every good gift came from Him.
teach: The Pilgrims gave thanks even after a hard year. Thanksgiving isn’t only for easy years. Psalm 100 tells us why we can always give thanks: “The Lord is good; His steadfast love endures forever.” His love never runs out.
q: What was the Pilgrims’ ship called? Who helped them?
Why did the Pilgrims give thanks even after a hard winter?
Psalm 100 says God’s faithfulness lasts “to all generations.” How has God been faithful to our family?
prayer: Lord God, You are good, and Your steadfast love endures forever. Thank You for our food, our home, our family and friends, and most of all for Jesus.
ask: Fill our hearts and our table with thankfulness today.

kids.lede: Happy Thanksgiving! The Lord is good, and His steadfast love endures forever!
quiz: Does God’s love ever run out?
Who gives us every good gift?
kids.draw: Draw your family’s Thanksgiving table.
mv: “For the LORD is good; his steadfast love endures forever.”

title: Hannah’s Prayer
verses: For this child I prayed, and the LORD has granted me my petition that I made to him.
story: A woman named Hannah wanted a baby more than anything. Year after year, she had no children, and another woman made fun of her for it. Hannah was so sad she cried and couldn’t eat.

One year, at the house of the Lord, Hannah prayed with her whole heart. She was praying so hard that her lips moved but no sound came out. The priest, Eli, thought something was wrong with her. Hannah said, “I’m pouring out my soul to the Lord.” She promised that if God gave her a son, she would give him to serve God all his life.

Eli said, “Go in peace. May God give you what you asked.” And God did! Hannah had a baby boy and named him Samuel. When he was old enough, she brought him to Eli to grow up serving in God’s house, just as she had promised. Then she sang a song of praise: “My heart rejoices in the Lord!”
teach: Hannah brought her deepest sadness to God and held nothing back. God loves it when we pour out our hearts to Him in prayer. He always hears, and He answers in the way that is best.
q: What did Hannah want more than anything? What did she name her son?
Why did Eli think something was wrong with Hannah? What was she really doing?
Hannah kept her promise even though it was hard. What does it look like to “pour out your heart” to God?
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for hearing Hannah’s prayer, and for hearing ours, even the ones too deep for words.
ask: Help us bring everything to You in prayer.

kids.lede: Hannah prayed with her whole heart for a baby. God answered, and she named him Samuel!
blanks: She prayed at the house of the ___.
quiz: Did God hear Hannah’s silent prayer?
kids.draw: Draw Hannah holding baby Samuel.

title: Speak, Lord
verses: And the LORD came and stood, calling as at other times, “Samuel! Samuel!” And Samuel said, “Speak, for your servant hears.”
story: Little Samuel grew up in the house of the Lord, helping old Eli the priest. One night, while Samuel was lying down near the lamp of God, he heard a voice: “Samuel!” He jumped up and ran to Eli. “Here I am! You called me.” But Eli said, “I didn’t call you. Go back to bed.”

It happened again. “Samuel!” He ran to Eli. “Here I am!” “I didn’t call you, my son. Lie down.” Then a third time. This time Eli understood: it was the Lord calling the boy! He told Samuel, “If He calls you again, say, ‘Speak, Lord, for Your servant hears.’”

Samuel lay down, and the Lord came and called, “Samuel! Samuel!” This time Samuel answered, “Speak, for Your servant hears.” And God told him important things. Samuel grew up to be a great prophet. The Lord was with him, and all Israel knew Samuel spoke God’s Word.
teach: God doesn’t usually call out loud in the night anymore. Today He speaks to us through His Word, the Bible. Every night at devotions, we can say what Samuel said: “Speak, Lord, for Your servant hears.”
q: How many times did God call Samuel? Who did Samuel think was calling?
What did Eli tell Samuel to say?
How does God speak to us today? What helps you listen?
prayer: Lord, speak to us through Your Word, for Your servants are listening. Thank You for calling Samuel, and for calling each of us by name.
ask: Help us listen to You and do what You say.

kids.lede: God called little Samuel in the night. Samuel said, “Speak, Lord, for Your servant hears!”
blanks: He heard a voice call his ___.
He thought it was Eli, but it was the ___.
God called him ___ times before he understood.
quiz: How does God speak to us today?
kids.draw: Draw Samuel listening in the night.

title: Hosanna!
verses: And the crowds that went before him and that followed him were shouting, “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
story: Today is the first Sunday of Advent, the start of a new church year. Advent means “coming.” For four weeks we get ready for Jesus’ coming at Christmas, and for His coming again at the end of time. Many families light the first candle on an Advent wreath tonight.

The Gospel reading for the first Sunday in Advent is a surprise: it isn’t about baby Jesus. It’s about Palm Sunday! Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a humble donkey, just as the prophet Zechariah said the King would come. Crowds spread their coats and palm branches on the road and shouted, “Hosanna! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”

“Hosanna” means “Save us now!” The people were welcoming their King. Advent starts here because it reminds us who the baby in the manger really is: the King who came to save us, riding humbly toward the cross.
teach: Every Sunday at church, right before the Lord’s Supper, we sing the same words the crowd shouted: “Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!” Because in the Supper, Jesus still comes to us.
q: What did Jesus ride into Jerusalem? What did the people shout?
What does “Hosanna” mean? What does “Advent” mean?
Why do you think the church begins Advent with Palm Sunday instead of the Christmas story?
prayer: Lord Jesus, our King, we welcome You! Hosanna! Thank You for coming humbly to save us.
ask: Prepare our hearts this Advent for Your coming.

kids.lede: Advent has begun! Jesus our King comes to us humbly, and we shout, “Hosanna!”
kids.draw: Draw an Advent wreath with one candle lit.
mv: “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!”

title: The Youngest Son
verses: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Do not look on his appearance or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him. For the LORD sees not as man sees: man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.”
story: Israel’s first king, Saul, stopped listening to God. So God sent Samuel, now an old prophet, to Bethlehem. “Go to the house of a man named Jesse. I have chosen one of his sons to be the next king.” Samuel took a horn of oil to anoint the new king.

Jesse brought out his oldest son, Eliab, who was tall and handsome. Samuel thought, “Surely this is the one!” But God said, “Don’t look at how tall he is. People look at the outside, but the Lord looks at the heart.” Seven sons walked by, and God said no to each one. “Are these all your sons?” Samuel asked.

“Well, there’s still the youngest, David. He’s out watching the sheep.” They sent for him. When the shepherd boy walked in, God said, “This is the one. Anoint him.” Samuel poured the oil on David’s head, and the Spirit of the Lord came on David from that day on. Bethlehem’s youngest shepherd would be king.
teach: God chose the one nobody expected. Years later, another King would be born in Bethlehem, in a stable, and many would overlook Him too. “Christ” means “Anointed One.” Jesus is the King God chose to save us.
q: Which town did Samuel go to? Where was David when they sent for him?
What does God look at instead of how people look?
David was anointed with oil; “Christ” means “Anointed One.” How does David’s story point to Jesus?
prayer: Lord God, thank You that You look at the heart. Thank You for choosing David, and for sending Jesus, the Anointed King, from David’s family.
ask: Help us see others the way You see them.

kids.lede: God chose David, the youngest shepherd, to be king. God looks at the heart!
blanks: Samuel went to the town of ___.
quiz: Did God choose the tallest son?
kids.draw: Draw Samuel pouring oil on David’s head.

title: David and Goliath
verses: Then David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword and with a spear and with a javelin, but I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.
story: The Philistine army had a champion named Goliath, a giant over nine feet tall with heavy bronze armor and a spear as thick as a tree branch. Every day he shouted at Israel’s army: “Send someone to fight me!” And every day, King Saul and all his soldiers were terrified.

Young David came to bring food to his brothers and heard Goliath mocking God. “Who is this man to defy the armies of the living God?” David told Saul, “I’ll fight him. God saved me from a lion and a bear when I protected my sheep. He’ll save me from this giant.” Saul offered his armor, but it was too big. David took only his shepherd’s staff, his sling, and five smooth stones.

Goliath sneered at the boy. But David said, “You come with a sword and spear, but I come in the name of the Lord.” David ran toward the giant, swung his sling, and the stone hit Goliath right in the forehead. The giant fell face down. Israel won, because the battle belonged to the Lord.
teach: David didn’t win because he was big or strong. He trusted God. Jesus, the Son of David, faced a much bigger enemy, sin, death, and the devil, and He won that battle for us on the cross.
q: What did David bring to fight Goliath? How many stones did he pick?
Why wasn’t David afraid when everyone else was?
What “giants” do people face today? How did Jesus, the Son of David, defeat the biggest giant of all?
prayer: Lord of hosts, thank You for giving David courage and victory. Thank You for Jesus, who defeated sin, death, and the devil for us.
ask: When we face giants, help us trust that the battle is Yours.

kids.lede: Young David fought the giant Goliath with a sling and a stone, in the name of the Lord!
blanks: David came in the name of the ___.
quiz: Who won the battle for David?
kids.draw: Draw David with his sling facing the giant.
mv: “I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts.”

title: The Lord Is My Shepherd
verses: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters.
He restores my soul. He leads me in paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
story: Before David was king, he was a shepherd. He knew exactly what sheep need. They need green grass to eat and calm water to drink, because sheep are scared of rushing water. They need someone to lead them on safe paths and protect them from wolves and bears. Without a shepherd, sheep get lost.

David also played the harp and wrote songs to God. One day he thought, “I take care of my sheep… and God takes care of me like that!” So he wrote the most famous psalm of all: “The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.”

In the psalm, the Shepherd feeds us, leads us, restores us when we’re worn out, and stays with us even in the darkest valley. He even prepares a table for us and fills our cup to overflowing. And David ends with a promise: “I shall dwell in the house of the Lord forever.”
teach: Jesus said, “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.” David protected his sheep from lions. Jesus gave His life for His sheep. That means you.
q: What did David take care of? What did he play?
What does a good shepherd do for his sheep?
Jesus calls Himself the Good Shepherd (John 10:11). What does He do that even David couldn’t?
prayer: Lord Jesus, You are our Good Shepherd. Thank You for feeding us, leading us, and laying down Your life for us.
ask: Lead us in Your paths and keep us close to You.

kids.lede: David wrote, “The Lord is my shepherd.” Jesus is our Good Shepherd who takes care of us!
quiz: Does the Shepherd leave us in the dark valley?
kids.draw: Draw the Good Shepherd with His sheep by still waters.
mv: “The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.”

title: Unto Us a Child Is Born
verses: For to us a child is born, to us a son is given; and the government shall be upon his shoulder, and his name shall be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
story: About 700 years before Jesus was born, God gave a prophet named Isaiah some amazing messages. Isaiah lived in a dark time. Enemies were attacking, kings were making bad choices, and people had turned away from God. Many people felt like they were walking in darkness.

But God gave Isaiah a promise of light: a child would be born, a son would be given. And this child would be no ordinary baby. He would be a King whose kingdom would grow forever. Isaiah listed His names, and each one tells us something about Him.

Wonderful Counselor: He knows exactly what we need. Mighty God: this baby would be God Himself! Everlasting Father: He would care for His people forever. Prince of Peace: He would make peace between God and people. The people waited seven hundred years. Then, one night in Bethlehem, the child was born.
teach: Isaiah 9:6 is one of the clearest promises of Jesus in the whole Old Testament. A baby who is also Mighty God: that’s the wonder of Christmas. God became a child for us. Many people hear these words every Christmas in Handel’s “Messiah.”
q: How long before Jesus did Isaiah live? Can you remember the four names?
Which of Jesus’ four names is your favorite? Why?
How can a baby be “Mighty God”? Why did God need to become a human to save us?
prayer: Lord Jesus, You are Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, and Prince of Peace. Thank You for being born for us.
ask: Be our counselor, our strength, and our peace.

kids.lede: Isaiah promised, “To us a child is born!” His names are Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace!
quiz: Is the baby Jesus also God?
kids.draw: Write Jesus’ four names in fancy letters and decorate them.
mv: “For to us a child is born, to us a son is given.”

title: Little Bethlehem
verses: But you, O Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are too little to be among the clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to be ruler in Israel, whose coming forth is from of old, from ancient days.
story: Around the same time as Isaiah, God sent another prophet named Micah. Micah warned the people about their sins: leaders who cheated the poor and people who said they loved God but didn’t act like it. He told them God wants us “to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God.”

But Micah also brought a promise, and it was very specific. The coming King wouldn’t be born in a big important city like Jerusalem. He would be born in Bethlehem, a tiny little town, David’s hometown, too small to be counted among the important places.

Seven hundred years later, wise men came looking for a newborn king. King Herod asked the Bible scholars, “Where is the Christ to be born?” And they read Micah’s words: “In Bethlehem.” God had told them exactly where, centuries ahead of time. And His “coming forth is from ancient days,” because Jesus existed before the world began.
teach: God loves to use small things: a small town, a shepherd boy, a baby in a manger. Your family might feel small too, but God does big things through little people and little places.
q: Which town did Micah say the King would come from? Whose hometown was it?
Why do you think God picked a tiny town instead of a big city?
How does Micah 5:2 show that Jesus existed before He was born in Bethlehem?
prayer: Faithful God, You keep every promise, right down to the town where Jesus would be born. Thank You for using small and humble things.
ask: Help us walk humbly with You and love kindness.

kids.lede: Micah promised that the King would be born in little Bethlehem, and that’s exactly where Jesus was born!
blanks: The King would be born in ___.
Bethlehem was too ___ to be important.
quiz: Did God tell the town ahead of time?
kids.draw: Draw the little town of Bethlehem at night under a star.
mv: “But you, O Bethlehem… from you shall come forth… one who is to be ruler.”

title: Jonah and the Big Fish
verses: But I with the voice of thanksgiving will sacrifice to you; what I have vowed I will pay. Salvation belongs to the LORD!”
story: God told the prophet Jonah, “Go to the big city of Nineveh and tell them to turn away from their evil.” But Jonah didn’t want to go. Nineveh was Israel’s enemy! So Jonah got on a ship going the opposite direction.

God sent a terrible storm. The sailors were terrified. Jonah said, “It’s my fault. Throw me into the sea, and it will be calm.” They did, and the sea went still. But God had a plan: He sent a huge fish to swallow Jonah! For three days and three nights Jonah was inside the fish. And there he prayed: “Salvation belongs to the Lord!”

God commanded the fish, and it spit Jonah out onto dry land. This time when God said “Go to Nineveh,” Jonah went. He preached, and the whole city, even the king, turned to God and said sorry. And God had mercy on them.
teach: Jesus said that just as Jonah was three days in the fish, He would be three days in the tomb (Matthew 12:40). Jonah came out alive; Jesus rose from the dead. And God’s mercy reaches even enemies like Nineveh, and people like us.
q: Where did God tell Jonah to go? What swallowed Jonah?
Why did Jonah run away? What did he pray inside the fish?
Jesus called His resurrection “the sign of Jonah.” How are their stories alike?
prayer: Merciful God, thank You for not giving up on Jonah, or on Nineveh, or on us. Salvation belongs to You!
ask: When we want to run from what You ask, turn us around.

kids.lede: Jonah ran from God and got swallowed by a big fish! God gave him another chance.
blanks: God told Jonah to go to ___.
Jonah got on a ___ going the other way.
quiz: Did Jonah obey God the first time?
How long was Jonah in the fish?
kids.draw: Draw Jonah inside the big fish.

title: Bishop Nicholas
verses: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
story: Today is St. Nicholas Day, the second Sunday of Advent. Long before Santa Claus, there was a real man named Nicholas. He lived about 300 years after Jesus in a city called Myra, in what is now Turkey. His parents died when he was young and left him money, and Nicholas decided to use it to help people in need. Later he became the bishop, the pastor, of Myra.

We don’t know every detail of his life, but many stories have been told about him for over 1,600 years. The most famous one: a poor father had three daughters and no money for them to get married. In those days, that meant a terrible future. So one night, Nicholas secretly tossed a bag of gold through their window. He did it again for the second daughter, and the third. Some say one bag landed in a stocking drying by the fire!

Old stories also say Nicholas stood up for what’s true. When some people taught that Jesus wasn’t truly God, he defended the faith that Jesus is fully God, and he was put in prison for being a Christian but never stopped trusting Jesus. Over many years, stories about him grew into the legend of Santa Claus.
teach: Nicholas gave in secret, just as Jesus taught, because he wasn’t trying to get attention. He gave because Jesus had given him everything. Christmas gifts remind us of the greatest gift: God giving His Son.
q: What did Nicholas toss through the window? How many daughters were there?
Why did Nicholas give in secret? How is the real Nicholas different from Santa?
Nicholas defended the truth that Jesus is God. Why does that matter for Christmas?
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for Bishop Nicholas and his generous heart. Thank You most of all for giving us Your Son.
ask: Help us give generously and quietly to people in need this Advent.

kids.lede: Bishop Nicholas secretly gave gold to a poor family. He gave because Jesus gave him everything!
blanks: Nicholas lived in the city of ___.
kids.draw: Draw a secret gift you could give someone this week.
mv: “Your Father who sees in secret will reward you.”

title: Fire from Heaven
verses: And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces and said, “The LORD, he is God; the LORD, he is God.”
story: Israel had a wicked king named Ahab, who worshiped a fake god called Baal. God sent His prophet Elijah to challenge Baal’s 450 prophets on Mount Carmel. “Let’s each build an altar and put a sacrifice on it. Don’t light the fire. The God who answers by fire, He is God.”

The prophets of Baal went first. From morning until noon they shouted, “O Baal, answer us!” They danced and yelled. Nothing happened. Elijah teased them: “Shout louder! Maybe he’s asleep!” They shouted all afternoon. Still nothing. No voice. No answer.

Then Elijah rebuilt the Lord’s altar with twelve stones and had the people pour water over it, three times, until it was soaked and the trench was full. Then Elijah prayed a simple prayer: “Lord, let them know that You are God.” Fire fell from heaven and burned up the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, and even the water! The people fell on their faces: “The Lord, He is God!”
teach: The very last Old Testament book, Malachi, promised God would send “Elijah” before the Lord came. Jesus said John the Baptist was that Elijah, the one who would get people ready for Jesus. That’s why Elijah shows up in Advent.
q: How many prophets of Baal were there? What did Elijah pour on his altar?
Why did Elijah have them pour water on the altar?
Baal never answered because he wasn’t real. What “fake gods” do people trust in today?
prayer: Lord God, You alone are God, and You answer when we pray. Thank You for sending prophets like Elijah to call people back to You.
ask: Turn our hearts away from fake gods and toward You.

kids.lede: Elijah prayed, and God sent fire from heaven! The people shouted, “The Lord, He is God!”
blanks: The people said, “The Lord, He is ___!”
kids.draw: Draw fire falling from heaven on Elijah’s altar.

title: Zechariah Can’t Talk
verses: But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.
story: An old priest named Zechariah and his wife Elizabeth loved God, but they had no children, and now they were too old. One day Zechariah was chosen to go into the holy place of the temple to burn incense, something a priest might get to do only once in his whole life.

Suddenly, right beside the altar, stood an angel! Zechariah was terrified. The angel said, “Don’t be afraid. Your prayer has been heard. Elizabeth will have a son, and you will name him John. He will get people ready for the Lord.” Zechariah said, “How can I be sure? We’re too old!”

The angel answered, “I am Gabriel. I stand in the presence of God. Because you didn’t believe, you won’t be able to speak until it happens.” When Zechariah came out, he couldn’t say a word. He could only wave his hands. But God kept His promise: Elizabeth was going to have a baby.
teach: Zechariah had prayed for a child for years, maybe so long he’d given up. But God had heard every prayer. God’s timing isn’t ours. And this baby, John, would be the one to point to Jesus.
q: What was the angel’s name? What would the baby be named?
Zechariah had prayed for many years. Why do you think God waited? Is there something you’ve prayed about for a long time?
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for hearing every prayer, even ones we’ve almost given up on. Thank You for sending John to get people ready for Jesus.
ask: Give us faith to believe Your promises.

kids.lede: The angel Gabriel told Zechariah he would have a son named John. Zechariah couldn’t talk until it happened!
quiz: Did Zechariah believe the angel right away?
kids.draw: Draw Zechariah in the temple with the angel.
mv: “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard.”

title: Let It Be to Me
verses: And the angel said to her, “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus.
And Mary said, “Behold, I am the servant of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word.” And the angel departed from her.
story: Six months later, God sent Gabriel again, this time to a little town called Nazareth, to a young woman named Mary. She was engaged to marry a carpenter named Joseph, from King David’s family. Gabriel said, “Greetings, favored one! The Lord is with you!” Mary was confused. What could this mean?

“Don’t be afraid, Mary. You will have a son, and you will name Him Jesus. He will be great, the Son of the Most High. He will sit on David’s throne, and His kingdom will never end.” Mary asked, “How can this be, since I’m not married?” Gabriel said, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you. The child will be called the Son of God. Nothing is impossible with God.”

Mary could have argued or been scared. Instead, she said, “I am the Lord’s servant. Let it be to me as you have said.” Mary trusted God’s Word. And right then, God’s Son began to grow inside her. God was becoming a human being.
teach: Zechariah asked, “How can I be sure?” Mary asked, “How will this happen?” and then she believed. Mary’s faith wasn’t in herself. It was in God’s Word. That’s our faith too: “Let it be to me according to Your word.”
q: What town did Mary live in? What name did Gabriel say to give the baby?
What did Mary say after the angel explained?
Mary’s answer is a model of faith. What makes it different from Zechariah’s? What would it look like to say “let it be to me” in your own life?
prayer: Lord God, nothing is impossible with You. Thank You for Mary’s faith, and for sending Your Son to be born as one of us.
ask: Give us faith to say, “Let it be to me according to Your word.”

kids.lede: The angel Gabriel told Mary she would be the mother of Jesus. Mary said, “I am the servant of the Lord!”
blanks: Mary said, “I am the ___ of the Lord.”
kids.draw: Draw Mary and the angel Gabriel.
mv: “Behold, I am the servant of the Lord.”

title: The Baby Who Jumped
verses: And Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord,
and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior,
story: After the angel’s visit, Mary hurried to the hill country to visit her relative Elizabeth, who was going to have baby John. It was a long trip, but Mary couldn’t wait to see her.

When Mary walked in and said hello, something amazing happened: baby John jumped inside Elizabeth! The Holy Spirit filled Elizabeth, and she shouted, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the baby you carry! Why am I so honored that the mother of my Lord comes to me?” Even before he was born, John was already rejoicing about Jesus!

Mary was so full of joy that she sang a song. It begins, “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior.” She sang about how God lifts up the humble and fills the hungry with good things. The church still sings Mary’s song, called the Magnificat, at evening prayer.
teach: John wasn’t born yet, but he already knew Jesus was near. Babies, even unborn babies, are precious to God. And Jesus brings joy to everyone near Him.
q: Who did Mary visit? What did baby John do?
What did Elizabeth call Mary’s baby?
Mary called God “my Savior.” Why did even Mary need a Savior? What does it mean to “magnify” the Lord?
prayer: Lord God, our souls magnify You and our spirits rejoice in You, our Savior. Thank You for every baby, born and unborn.
ask: Fill us with the joy of Jesus this Advent.

kids.lede: Baby John jumped for joy inside Elizabeth when Mary came to visit! Mary sang a song of praise.
quiz: Did baby John know Jesus was near?
kids.draw: Draw Mary and Elizabeth hugging.
mv: “My spirit rejoices in God my Savior.”

title: His Name Is John
verses: And he asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” And they all wondered.
And immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue loosed, and he spoke, blessing God.
story: The day came, and Elizabeth had her baby boy. All the neighbors and relatives were so happy for her. Eight days later, they gathered to name him. Everyone said, “Call him Zechariah, after his father.”

But Elizabeth said, “No. His name is John.” “But nobody in your family has that name!” So they made signs to Zechariah, who still couldn’t talk. He asked for a writing tablet and wrote: “His name is John.” Everyone was amazed.

And at that very moment, Zechariah could talk again! The first thing he did was praise God. He sang a song, filled with the Holy Spirit: “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for He has visited and redeemed His people!” Then he looked at his baby son: “And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High. You will go before the Lord to prepare His ways.”
teach: Zechariah’s song, the Benedictus, is sung in the church’s morning prayer. John’s whole job in life was to point to Jesus. That’s a good job for us, too.
q: What did everyone want to name the baby? What did Zechariah write?
What was the first thing Zechariah did when he could talk again?
John’s job was to “prepare the way” for Jesus. How can we point others to Jesus?
prayer: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for He has visited and redeemed His people! Thank You for giving Zechariah his voice back to praise You.
ask: Use our voices to praise You and point others to Jesus.

kids.lede: Zechariah wrote, “His name is John!” and he could talk again. He sang praise to God!
blanks: John would ___ the way for Jesus.
quiz: What was the first thing Zechariah did when he could talk?
kids.draw: Draw Zechariah writing on his tablet, “His name is John.”

title: Joseph’s Dream
verses: But as he considered these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary as your wife, for that which is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
She will bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.”
story: Joseph the carpenter was engaged to Mary. When he found out she was going to have a baby, he was heartbroken and confused. He knew it wasn’t his baby. Joseph was a good man, and he didn’t want to embarrass Mary, so he decided to break off the engagement quietly.

But while he was thinking about it, an angel came to him in a dream. “Joseph, son of David, don’t be afraid to take Mary as your wife. The baby is from the Holy Spirit. She will have a son, and you will name Him Jesus, because He will save His people from their sins.” The name Jesus means “The Lord saves.”

When Joseph woke up, he did exactly what the angel said. He married Mary and took care of her. When the baby was born, Joseph named Him Jesus. The Bible never records a single word Joseph spoke. But it tells us over and over what he did: he trusted and obeyed.
teach: Joseph is a great example for dads, and for everyone. He didn’t make speeches. He listened to God and did what God said, protecting Mary and Jesus. God chose Joseph to be Jesus’ earthly father.
q: What did the angel tell Joseph in his dream? What does the name Jesus mean?
Joseph was confused and hurt at first. How did he show faith?
The Bible records none of Joseph’s words, only his actions. What does quiet, obedient faith look like at home?
prayer: Lord God, thank You for Joseph, who trusted You and protected Mary and Jesus. Thank You for Jesus, who saves us from our sins.
ask: Give our family quiet, faithful hearts that listen and obey.

kids.lede: An angel told Joseph in a dream, “Name the baby Jesus, for He will save His people from their sins.”
blanks: An angel came to him in a ___.
Jesus will save His people from their ___.
quiz: What does the name Jesus mean?
kids.draw: Draw Joseph asleep, dreaming of the angel.
mv: “He will save his people from their sins.”

title: Behold, the Lamb of God
verses: Isa 40:3
A voice cries: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD; make straight in the desert a highway for our God.
John 1:29
The next day he saw Jesus coming toward him, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
story: Today is the third Sunday of Advent. Baby John grew up and went to live in the wilderness. He wore clothes of camel’s hair and ate locusts and wild honey! He was the voice Isaiah promised, crying in the wilderness, “Prepare the way of the Lord!”

Crowds came out from the cities to hear him. John told them, “Repent! Turn away from your sins, because the kingdom of heaven is near.” People confessed their sins, and John baptized them in the Jordan River. Some people wondered, “Is John the Christ?” But John said, “No. Someone is coming who is greater than I am. I’m not even worthy to untie His sandals.”

Then one day, John saw Jesus walking toward him. John pointed and shouted, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” That was John’s whole job: point to Jesus. “He must increase, but I must decrease.”
teach: We sing John’s words in church before the Lord’s Supper: “Lamb of God, You take away the sin of the world; have mercy on us.” Advent is a time to repent and get ready, like John said, because the Lamb is coming.
q: What did John eat? Where did he baptize people?
What did John say when he saw Jesus?
John said, “He must increase, but I must decrease.” What does that mean for us?
prayer: Lamb of God, You take away the sin of the world; have mercy on us. Thank You for John, who pointed the way to You.
ask: Prepare our hearts this Advent to receive You.

kids.lede: John the Baptist pointed to Jesus and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God!”
blanks: He baptized people in the ___ River.
John said, “Prepare the ___ of the Lord!”
kids.draw: Draw John the Baptist pointing to Jesus.
mv: “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!”

title: A Shoot from a Stump
verses: There shall come forth a shoot from the stump of Jesse, and a branch from his roots shall bear fruit.
And the Spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him, the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
story: Remember Jesse, David’s father? From Jesse’s family came King David and many kings after him. But over the years, the kings turned away from God, and finally enemies conquered Jerusalem. David’s royal family was like a great tree that had been chopped down. Only a stump was left.

But Isaiah gave a promise: from that dead-looking stump, a little green shoot would grow! A new King would come from Jesse’s family, and God’s Spirit would rest on Him. He would be wise and fair. He would care for the poor. And under His rule, the wolf would lie down with the lamb, and a little child would lead them.

For hundreds of years, it looked like the stump was dead. But God hadn’t forgotten. Jesus was born from the family of Jesse and David. He is the shoot from the stump. Many families make a “Jesse tree” in Advent, hanging an ornament for each Bible story that leads up to Jesus, from creation to Christmas.
teach: When things look dead and hopeless, God can make something new grow. That’s what He did through Jesus, and it’s what He does in our lives too. The whole Old Testament is like a family tree growing toward Jesus.
q: What was left after the tree was chopped down? What grew out of it?
What will it be like when the new King rules, according to Isaiah?
Look back at all the stories we’ve read since October. How do they make a “Jesse tree” leading to Jesus?
prayer: Lord God, You made new life grow from the stump of Jesse. Thank You for Jesus, the King who rules with wisdom and love.
ask: Where things feel dead or hopeless, make new life grow.

blanks: The tree was cut down to a ___.
quiz: Who is the shoot from Jesse?

mv: “There shall come forth a shoot from the stump of Jesse.”

title: Jesus’ Family Tree
verses: The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
story: The very first page of the New Testament might look boring: a long list of names. “Abraham was the father of Isaac, and Isaac the father of Jacob, and Jacob the father of Judah…” But it’s actually one of the most amazing pages in the Bible. It’s Jesus’ family tree.

Look closely and you’ll find people we’ve met: Abraham who counted the stars, Isaac on the mountain, Jacob with his ladder, Judah who offered his life for Benjamin, and David the shepherd king. God kept His promises through every generation.

But you’ll also find surprises. There’s Rahab, a woman from Jericho, and Ruth, a woman from Moab. Neither one was an Israelite, but God brought them into His family. There are kings who did terrible things. Jesus’ family tree is full of sinners and outsiders. Jesus didn’t come from a perfect family. He came into a real, messy family, because He came to save real, messy people.
teach: Matthew includes the scandals on purpose. Jesus isn’t ashamed to call sinners His family. Hebrews 2:11 says He is not ashamed to call us brothers and sisters.
q: Name some people from Jesus’ family tree we’ve read about.
Why would Matthew start his Gospel with a family tree?
Jesus’ family tree includes sinners and outsiders. What does that tell you about the kind of people Jesus came for?
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for coming into a real family full of real sinners, and for not being ashamed to call us Your family.
ask: Thank You for our family, and for all the generations who passed down the faith to us.

Jesus is not ___ to call us family.

kids.draw: Draw your own family tree with names on the branches.
mv: “The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ.”

title: Comfort, Comfort My People
verses: Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.
He will tend his flock like a shepherd; he will gather the lambs in his arms; he will carry them in his bosom, and gently lead those that are with young.
story: God’s people had been through a very hard time. Enemies had taken them far from home, to Babylon. Daniel and his friends were part of that time. The people felt forgotten. They thought, “God must be done with us.”

But God told Isaiah to bring a new message, a gentle one: “Comfort, comfort My people. Speak tenderly to them. Tell them their hard time is over and their sins are forgiven.” God wasn’t done with them at all!

Isaiah described God like a shepherd who picks up the little lambs that can’t keep up, carries them close to His heart, and walks slowly with the mother sheep. God isn’t rough or in a hurry. He is gentle with the weak and the little ones.
teach: Some people think of God as angry or far away. But Isaiah shows us a God who scoops up little lambs and carries them close. That’s exactly who Jesus is. He took children in His arms and blessed them.
q: What does God tell Isaiah to say? What does the shepherd do with the little lambs?
Why did God’s people feel forgotten?
How does Isaiah 40 change the way you picture God? When do you need God to carry you?
prayer: Gentle Shepherd, thank You for comforting Your people and carrying the little lambs. Thank You for forgiving our sins.
ask: When we are tired or sad, carry us close to Your heart.

kids.lede: God said, “Comfort, comfort My people!” He carries the little lambs close to His heart.
blanks: He will tend His ___ like a shepherd.
He carries the ___ in His arms.
quiz: Is God rough with little lambs?
Where does the shepherd carry the lambs?
kids.draw: Draw the shepherd carrying a lamb in his arms.
mv: “Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.”

title: God with Us
verses: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
story: For more than a thousand years, starting on December 17, Christians have sung seven special prayers called the “O Antiphons,” one each night until Christmas Eve. Each one calls Jesus by an Old Testament name: O Wisdom, O Lord, O Root of Jesse, O Key of David, O Dayspring, O King of the Nations, and O Emmanuel.

Later, those prayers were made into a hymn you probably know: “O Come, O Come, Emmanuel.” Its verses pray, “O come, Thou Rod of Jesse’s stem… O come, Thou Dayspring from on high… O come, Thou Key of David, come.” It’s a song of waiting, sung by people longing for the Savior.

The last name, Emmanuel (or Immanuel), comes from tonight’s verse. Seven hundred years before Jesus, Isaiah said a virgin would have a son and name Him Immanuel, which means “God with us.” And Matthew tells us that this came true when Mary had baby Jesus. God didn’t stay far away. He came to be with us.
teach: “God with us” is the heart of Christmas. God didn’t send a message or an angel to fix things. He came Himself. And Jesus’ last promise in Matthew is, “I am with you always, to the end of the age.”
q: What does Emmanuel mean? What hymn uses the O Antiphons?
Why is it good news that God came to be with us instead of staying far away?
Jesus’ name Emmanuel appears at the start of Matthew, and His promise “I am with you always” at the end. Why do you think Matthew bookends his Gospel that way?
prayer: O come, O come, Emmanuel! Thank You, Lord Jesus, for coming to be God with us.
ask: Be with us always, in every day and every night.

title: A Great Light
verses: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; those who dwelt in a land of deep darkness, on them has light shone.
story: These are the darkest days of the whole year. The sun sets early and rises late. On Monday it will be the longest night of the year. Long ago, before electricity, the dark of winter could feel scary and long.

Isaiah used that picture to describe the world without God: people walking in darkness, unable to see where they’re going, afraid and lost. Sin is like darkness. It makes us stumble, and it hides us from God and from each other.

But Isaiah promised a great light would shine. And when Jesus grew up, He said, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows Me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.” That’s why we light candles at Christmas. Jesus is the light that came into the darkest night.
teach: Every Advent candle we light makes the room a little brighter, until Christmas when the Christ candle is lit. Jesus is the light no darkness can put out (John 1:5).
q: What is the longest night of the year? Who is the light of the world?
John 1:5 says the darkness has not overcome the light. What dark things in the world does Jesus’ light shine into?
prayer: Lord Jesus, You are the light of the world. Thank You for shining into our darkness.
ask: Help us walk in Your light and shine it for others.

kids.lede: Isaiah promised, “The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light!” Jesus is the light of the world!
blanks: Jesus is the light of the ___.
quiz: Who is the light of the world?
kids.draw: Draw a candle shining in a dark room.
mv: “The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.”

title: The Road to Bethlehem
verses: In those days a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be registered.
And Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the town of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and lineage of David,
to be registered with Mary, his betrothed, who was with child.
story: Far away in Rome, the most powerful man in the world, Caesar Augustus, decided to count all the people in his empire, probably so he could collect more taxes. He gave an order: everyone had to go to their family’s hometown to be counted.

Joseph’s family came from King David, so he had to go to Bethlehem, David’s town. That was about 90 miles from Nazareth, mostly walking, up and down hills. And Mary was going to have her baby very soon! The trip probably took about a week.

Caesar thought he was in charge. But God was using Caesar’s order to bring Mary and Joseph to exactly the right place. Remember Micah’s promise? The King would be born in Bethlehem. God can use even the decisions of emperors to keep His promises.
teach: Mary and Joseph didn’t choose this trip, and it was hard. But God was guiding every step. When our plans get interrupted, God is still working out His plans.
q: Who made everyone go to their hometown? Which town did Mary and Joseph go to?
Why was the trip so hard for Mary?
Caesar thought he was in charge. How did God use Caesar’s order to keep Micah’s promise?
prayer: Lord God, You guided Mary and Joseph every step of the way to Bethlehem. Thank You that You are in charge of everything.
ask: When our plans change, help us trust that You are guiding us.

kids.lede: Mary and Joseph traveled to Bethlehem, just as God promised. God was guiding every step!
blanks: Everyone had to go to be ___.
Mary was going to have a ___.
kids.draw: Draw Mary and Joseph on the road to Bethlehem.
mv: “To the city of David, which is called Bethlehem.”

title: The First Advent Wreath
verses: Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, rejoice.
Let your reasonableness be known to everyone. The Lord is at hand;
story: Today is the fourth and last Sunday of Advent. Tonight all four candles on the Advent wreath are lit. But where did the Advent wreath come from? About 185 years ago, in Hamburg, Germany, there was a Lutheran pastor named Johann Wichern who ran a home for poor and orphaned boys.

Every December, the boys kept asking, “Is it Christmas yet? How many more days?” So in 1839, Pastor Wichern took an old wagon wheel and put a candle on it for every day until Christmas, more than twenty of them: little red ones for the weekdays and four big white ones for the Sundays. Every day at prayer time, the boys lit one more candle, and the room got brighter and brighter as Christmas came closer.

Other families loved the idea. Over time, the wheel became a circle of evergreen branches, and the candles became just four, one for each Sunday. Now churches and families all over the world light Advent wreaths. It all started with a Lutheran pastor who loved some kids and wanted to help them wait for Jesus.
teach: Tonight’s verse says, “Rejoice in the Lord always… The Lord is at hand.” The waiting is almost over! The circle of the wreath has no end, like God’s love, and the growing light reminds us that Jesus, the light of the world, is coming.
q: What did Pastor Wichern use for the first Advent wreath? What colors were the candles?
Why did he make it? How did the room change each day?
Why is an evergreen circle a good picture of God’s love and of Jesus?
prayer: Lord Jesus, we rejoice, because You are near! Thank You for Pastor Wichern, who helped children wait for You.
ask: Help us wait with joy these last few days before Christmas.

title: My Lord and My God
verses: Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!”
Jesus said to him, “Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.”
story: Today the church remembers St. Thomas, one of Jesus’ twelve disciples. After Jesus rose from the dead on Easter, He appeared to the disciples. But Thomas wasn’t there. When the others said, “We have seen the Lord!” Thomas said, “Unless I see the nail marks in His hands and put my finger in them, I will never believe.”

A week later, the disciples were together again, and this time Thomas was with them. The doors were locked, but suddenly Jesus was standing there! “Peace be with you.” Then He turned to Thomas. “Put your finger here and see My hands. Stop doubting and believe.”

Thomas didn’t need to touch anything. He fell down and said, “My Lord and my God!” It’s one of the clearest confessions in the whole Bible that Jesus is God. And Jesus said, “You believe because you have seen. Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.” That means us!
teach: Thomas called Jesus “my God.” In four days we celebrate the birthday of that same God, born as a baby. The baby in the manger is the risen Lord. And Jesus calls us blessed, because we believe without seeing.
q: What did Thomas want to see before he believed? What did he say when he saw Jesus?
Jesus said people who believe without seeing are blessed. Who is He talking about?
Thomas had doubts, and Jesus came to him. What do you do with your own doubts?
prayer: Lord Jesus, You are our Lord and our God. Thank You for coming to Thomas in his doubts, and for coming to us through Your Word.
ask: When we have doubts, help our unbelief.

title: Silent Night
verses: because of the tender mercy of our God, whereby the sunrise shall visit us from on high
to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.”
story_title: A song for a quiet night
story: Christmas is almost here! In a little village in Austria called Oberndorf, there was a church named St. Nicholas. Its young assistant priest, Joseph Mohr, had written a poem a couple of years earlier about the night Jesus was born. It began, “Silent night, holy night, all is calm, all is bright.”

On Christmas Eve in 1818, Mohr walked to the home of his friend Franz Gruber, a schoolteacher who played the church organ. He asked Gruber to write a tune for his poem that could be sung with just a guitar. Some say the organ was broken that winter. Gruber wrote the melody that same day.

That night, at the end of the Christmas Eve service, Mohr played his guitar, and the two men sang the new carol for the first time. Organ repairmen and traveling singers carried it to other towns, and today “Silent Night” is sung in hundreds of languages all over the world. One verse says, “Son of God, love’s pure light, radiant beams from Thy holy face.”
teach: Tonight’s verse is from Zechariah’s song. He promised that God would send “the sunrise from on high” to shine on people sitting in darkness and to guide our feet into peace. That sunrise is Jesus. “Silent Night” sings about that same light and peace, and in two more nights, we celebrate His birth.
q: Where was “Silent Night” first sung? What instrument was played?
Why do you think this simple song became so loved all over the world?
Zechariah called Jesus “the sunrise from on high.” What darkness does Jesus shine into? What peace does He bring?
prayer: Lord Jesus, love’s pure light, thank You for coming like the sunrise to shine on people in darkness. Thank You for songs that tell the world about You.
ask: Guide our feet into the way of peace, and quiet our hearts as Christmas comes.

quiz: What instrument played “Silent Night” the first time?

title: From Heaven Above
verses: But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth his Son, born of woman, born under the law,
to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as sons.
story: Martin Luther and his wife Katie had a house full of children, and Luther loved Christmas with his family. Around the year 1534, he wrote a Christmas hymn just for them to sing at home on Christmas Eve. It’s called “From Heaven Above to Earth I Come.”

The first verses are sung by the angel, as if he were flying down to the shepherds: “From heaven above to earth I come, to bring good news to everyone! Glad tidings of great joy I bring, whereof I now will sing and say.” Then the rest of the hymn is the family answering: “Let us be glad and go see what God has given us, His only Son!”

Luther wrote fifteen verses! They tell the whole Christmas story for children: the baby in the manger, the Lord of all wrapped in rags, the King of kings lying on hay. And the hymn ends with the whole family singing praise: “Glory to God in highest heaven, who unto us His Son has given!”
teach: Paul says God sent His Son “when the fullness of time had come.” God had been promising a Savior since the garden of Eden, and He sent Jesus at exactly the right moment. Jesus came to make us God’s own children. Tomorrow night, the waiting is over.
q: Who wrote “From Heaven Above”? Who did he write it for?
Who sings the first verses of the hymn? Who answers?
Galatians says Jesus came so we could be adopted as God’s children. What does it mean to be adopted into God’s family?
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for sending Your Son at just the right time, and for making us Your children. Thank You for Martin Luther and his Christmas hymn for children.
ask: Get our hearts ready to welcome Jesus tomorrow night.

quiz: Who did Luther write the hymn for?

title: Born in Bethlehem
verses: And while they were there, the time came for her to give birth.
And she gave birth to her firstborn son and wrapped him in swaddling cloths and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the inn.
story: Mary and Joseph finally arrived in Bethlehem, tired from their long trip. But the town was packed with people who had come to be counted. Every guest room was full. There was no place for them to stay.

So they stayed in a place where animals were kept. And there, that very night, Mary’s baby was born. She wrapped Him snugly in strips of cloth, called swaddling cloths, and laid Him in a manger, the feeding box for the animals, filled with hay.

It was the most important birth in all of history, and it happened quietly, among animals, with no doctor and no crowd. The Son of God, who made the stars, was now a tiny baby who needed His mother to feed Him. God kept every promise: born of a virgin, from David’s family, in little Bethlehem. Emmanuel, God with us, had come.
teach: Martin Luther loved to marvel that the God who holds the whole world was held in Mary’s arms. In the hymn he wrote for his children, “From Heaven Above,” one verse says, “Ah, dearest Jesus, holy Child, make Thee a bed, soft, undefiled, within my heart, that it may be a quiet chamber kept for Thee.”
q: Why couldn’t Mary and Joseph find a room? Where did Mary lay baby Jesus?
Which promises from Advent came true tonight?
Why would God choose to be born so humbly? What does that tell us about Him?
prayer: Dearest Jesus, holy Child, thank You for being born for us in Bethlehem. Make Your home in our hearts.
ask: Bless our family and all our celebrations this Christmas.

title: Good News of Great Joy
verses: And the angel said to them, “Fear not, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy that will be for all the people.
For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
“Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among those with whom he is pleased!”
story: Merry Christmas! On the night Jesus was born, there were shepherds out in the fields near Bethlehem, the same hills where young David once watched his sheep. Shepherds weren’t important people. They worked outside day and night, and many people looked down on them.

Suddenly an angel appeared, and God’s glory blazed all around them. The shepherds were terrified! But the angel said, “Fear not! I bring you good news of great joy for all the people. Unto you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, who is Christ the Lord. You will find a baby wrapped in swaddling cloths and lying in a manger.” Then the whole sky filled with angels singing, “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace!”

The shepherds said, “Let’s go to Bethlehem and see!” They hurried and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in the manger, just as the angel said. Then they told everyone what they had heard, and went back to their sheep praising God. But Mary was quiet. She treasured up all these things, pondering them in her heart.
teach: The angel didn’t say, “A Savior is born for the world in general.” He said, “Unto you.” God told shepherds first, ordinary people, to show that Jesus is for everyone, and for you. John’s Gospel says it this way: “The Word became flesh and dwelt among us.” Today, like Mary, take a moment in all the busyness to treasure that.
q: Who heard the news first? Where did the angel say they would find the baby?
What did the shepherds do after they saw Jesus? What did Mary do?
The angel said “unto you.” Why does it matter that Jesus was born for you personally? What will you treasure from this Christmas?
prayer: Lord Jesus, Savior, Christ the Lord, thank You for being born for us! Glory to God in the highest! Merry Christmas, Jesus!
ask: Help us treasure You above every gift today, and tell others the good news.

title: Stephen Forgives
verses: And as they were stoning Stephen, he called out, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.”
And falling to his knees he cried out with a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” And when he had said this, he fell asleep.
story: The day after Christmas is St. Stephen’s Day. After Jesus went back to heaven, the church grew quickly. The apostles chose seven men to help care for widows and hand out food fairly. One of them was Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, who also preached about Jesus with great wisdom.

Some leaders hated what Stephen taught. They dragged him before the council. Stephen bravely told the whole story of God’s people, from Abraham to Joseph to Moses, all pointing to Jesus. The leaders got so angry they rushed at him. Stephen looked up and said, “I see heaven opened, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God!”

They threw Stephen out of the city and stoned him. And as he was dying, Stephen prayed just like Jesus did on the cross: “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” He forgave the people hurting him. A young man named Saul was watching. Later, God would change Saul into the apostle Paul.
teach: The church puts Stephen right after Christmas to remind us why Jesus came. The baby in the manger grew up to give His life, and He gives His followers courage to forgive even their enemies. That’s also the day in the carol “Good King Wenceslas,” who went out “on the feast of Stephen” to help a poor man.
q: What job did Stephen do in the church? What did he see when he looked up?
Stephen prayed for the people hurting him. Who else prayed like that?
Why would the church remember a martyr the day after Christmas? Who might you need to forgive?
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for Stephen’s faith and courage. Thank You that heaven is open to us because of You.
ask: Give us hearts that forgive, even when it’s hard.

title: God Is Love
verses: In this the love of God was made manifest among us, that God sent his only Son into the world, so that we might live through him.
In this is love, not that we have loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.
story: Today the church remembers St. John, one of Jesus’ closest friends. John and his brother James were fishermen when Jesus called them. Jesus nicknamed them the “Sons of Thunder,” maybe because they had big tempers! John called himself “the disciple whom Jesus loved.”

John was at the Last Supper, leaning next to Jesus. He was the only disciple at the foot of the cross, and from the cross Jesus asked John to take care of His mother, Mary. On Easter morning, John ran to the empty tomb and believed.

John lived to be very old, longer than any other apostle. He wrote the Gospel of John, three letters, and the book of Revelation. An old story says that when he was too old to preach long sermons, he would be carried into church and just say, “Little children, love one another.” When people asked why he always said that, he answered, “Because it is the Lord’s command, and if this is done, it is enough.”
teach: The “Son of Thunder” became the apostle of love, because Jesus changed him. John says real love isn’t that we loved God first. It’s that God loved us and sent His Son. That’s the love of Christmas.
q: What was John’s job before he followed Jesus? What nickname did Jesus give him?
What did Jesus ask John to do from the cross?
John says love isn’t that we loved God, but that He loved us. Why is that order so important?
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for loving us first and sending Your Son. Thank You for St. John, who taught us about Your love.
ask: Little children that we are, help us love one another.

title: Wise Men and a Warning
verses: Now when they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, “Rise, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, and remain there until I tell you, for Herod is about to search for the child, to destroy him.”
story: After Jesus was born, wise men from the East saw a special star and followed it to Jerusalem. “Where is the one born King of the Jews? We’ve come to worship Him.” King Herod was furious and afraid. He didn’t want another king! He found out from the Bible scholars that the Christ would be born in Bethlehem, just as Micah said.

The star led the wise men to the house where Jesus was. They bowed down and gave Him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh. Then God warned them in a dream not to go back to Herod, so they went home a different way.

That night, an angel came to Joseph in a dream again: “Get up! Take the child and His mother and escape to Egypt. Herod wants to hurt the child.” Joseph got up in the middle of the night and left right away. Herod did something terrible to the little boys of Bethlehem, and the church remembers those children today. But God kept Jesus safe in Egypt, the same land where Joseph long ago had saved his family.
teach: Even at Christmas, the world had evil in it, like Herod. Jesus came into that real world to save it. Today the church remembers the children of Bethlehem, and trusts that Jesus holds every child who suffers.
q: What gifts did the wise men bring? Where did Joseph take Mary and Jesus?
How did God protect Jesus? How many times did Joseph listen to angels in dreams?
Why does it matter that Jesus came into a world with real evil in it?
prayer: Lord God, thank You for protecting baby Jesus and for sending Him into our broken world. Hold every child who is suffering today.
ask: Protect our children, and make us brave like Joseph.

title: Now I Can Go in Peace
verses: “Lord, now you are letting your servant depart in peace, according to your word;
for my eyes have seen your salvation
that you have prepared in the presence of all peoples,
a light for revelation to the Gentiles, and for glory to your people Israel.”
story: When Jesus was forty days old, Mary and Joseph brought Him to the temple in Jerusalem, as God’s law said to do for a firstborn son. They were poor, so they brought the poor family’s offering: two small birds.

In Jerusalem lived an old man named Simeon, who loved God and was waiting for the Savior. The Holy Spirit had promised him he would not die before he saw the Christ. That day, the Spirit led Simeon to the temple. When he saw Mary and Joseph with the baby, he knew. He took Jesus in his arms and praised God.

“Lord, now You can let Your servant go in peace, because my eyes have seen Your salvation, a light for all the nations!” Simeon had waited his whole life. Now he had held the Savior, and he was ready to die in peace. Then he blessed Mary and Joseph, who were amazed at what he said.
teach: Lutherans sing Simeon’s song, the Nunc Dimittis, after receiving the Lord’s Supper. Like Simeon, we have held our Savior: in the Supper, Jesus gives us His body and blood. Then we can go in peace, ready for whatever comes, even death.
q: How old was Jesus when He went to the temple? What did Simeon do when he saw Him?
What had the Holy Spirit promised Simeon?
We sing Simeon’s song after communion. How is receiving the Lord’s Supper like Simeon holding Jesus?
prayer: Lord, our eyes have seen Your salvation in Jesus. Thank You for Simeon, who waited faithfully, and for letting us receive Jesus in Your Word and Supper.
ask: Let us go in peace, according to Your Word.

title: Anna Tells Everyone
verses: And coming up at that very hour she began to give thanks to God and to speak of him to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.
story: At the same time Simeon was holding baby Jesus, someone else walked up. Her name was Anna, and she was very old: 84 years old! Her husband had died long ago, and ever since, she had stayed at the temple, worshiping God night and day, praying and fasting.

When Anna saw baby Jesus, she knew who He was right away. She started thanking God out loud! Then she did something wonderful: she went and told everyone who was waiting for the Savior. “He’s here! The one we’ve been waiting for is here!”
Like the shepherds, Anna couldn’t keep the good news to herself. She didn’t have to be young or strong or famous. She just told people what she had seen.
teach: You don’t have to be grown-up to tell people about Jesus. Anna was old, the shepherds were ordinary, and kids can do it too. That’s what “Go, Tell It on the Mountain” is all about.
q: How old was Anna? Where did she spend her time?
What did Anna do after she saw Jesus?
Who is someone you could tell about Jesus? What would you say?
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for faithful Anna, who prayed for so many years and then told everyone about You.
ask: Give us joy to tell others about You, too.

title: New Every Morning
verses: The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases; his mercies never come to an end;
they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
story: Tonight is the last night of the year. Tomorrow is a brand-new year. It’s a good time to look back and remember all the ways God has been faithful to our family.

Think about all the stories we’ve read since October: Luther discovering grace, Abraham under the stars, Joseph in the pit and the palace, Moses at the Red Sea, David and the giant, the prophets’ promises, the angels and shepherds, and the baby in the manger. In every single story, God kept His promises. He never gave up on His people.

Tonight’s verse was written by the prophet Jeremiah during one of the saddest times in Israel’s history, after Jerusalem had been destroyed. Even then, he wrote, “The steadfast love of the Lord never ceases. His mercies are new every morning. Great is Your faithfulness.” Whatever this new year brings, God’s mercy will be waiting for us every single morning.
teach: We don’t know what the new year holds, but we know who holds it. Jesus says, “I am with you always.” Every morning He gives fresh mercy and forgiveness. That’s a good way to start a new year.
q: What was your favorite story from our devotions this fall? What are you thankful for from this year?
Jeremiah wrote this verse in a very sad time. Why is that important?
What do you want to ask God for in the new year? How have you seen God be faithful this year?
prayer: Faithful God, thank You for this whole year: for every good gift, for carrying us through hard days, and for Your mercy that is new every morning.
ask: Lead our families into the new year with You. Keep us gathering around Your Word together.

kids.lede: God’s mercies are new every morning! Happy New Year!

kids.draw: Draw your favorite Bible story from this fall.
mv: “They are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.”
